findings.finding: RND.PT.realtime (real-time path tracing, ReSTIR PT class) is marked E while RND.GI.restir (ReSTIR GI & path-traced GI) is M and on the radar. The same technique has two maturity classes. Because E entries need no radar row, real-time PT has no revisit trigger and no fallback, and RND.GI.rt-required inherits the false E.
findings.evidence: Shipped PT modes (Cyberpunk 2077 RT Overdrive, Alan Wake 2) are top-end-GPU-only and depend on vendor ray-reconstruction denoisers (RND.RECON.ml-denoise is M). ReSTIR PT (Lin et al., SIGGRAPH 2022) is still evolving and no console-class title ships it.
findings.proposed_change: Set RND.PT.realtime to M and add a radar entry with fallback RND.GI.hybrid/probes and revisit trigger 'console-class budget without vendor-only denoiser'. Keep RND.PT.reference and RND.PT.offline as E.

findings.target: atmosphere-weather, terrain, vegetation-foliage, C-SCENETEX, C-COLOR, C-RT, C-LIGHT, RND.RT.instances
findings.finding: atmosphere-weather owns the media integrator, clouds and sky but consumes neither C-SCENETEX (depth/velocity) nor C-COLOR (pre-exposure) nor C-GI. terrain consumes no C-LIGHT, C-GI, C-RT or C-SCENETEX, and vegetation-foliage no C-SCENETEX or C-GI. Participation of terrain, water and vegetation in TLAS, SDF scenes and surface caches is unowned: RND.RT.instances and RND.RT.lod name only virtualized-geometry-lod, and terrain-render lists only geometry-pipeline as contributor. check.py cannot see implicit use.
findings.evidence: Sky, cloud and froxel passes read scene depth and write pre-exposed color (Hillaire, Frostbite atmosphere/cloud talks; UE Volumetric Cloud/Height Fog). Heightfield terrain in a hybrid-GI/RT scene needs BLAS or SDF proxies (UE Lumen landscape cards; terrain in TLAS in open-world titles).
findings.proposed_change: Add C-SCENETEX?, C-COLOR?, C-GI? to atmosphere-weather consumes; C-LIGHT?, C-RT?, C-GI?, C-SCENETEX? to terrain; C-SCENETEX? to vegetation-foliage. Add terrain, water-ocean and vegetation-foliage as contributors of RND.RT.instances and RND.RT.lod. Add capability WLD.ENV.terrain-rt (heightfield/clipmap to BLAS/SDF proxy), owner terrain, contributor ray-tracing-infrastructure.

findings.target: RND.LOD, WLD.ENV.vegetation, RND.GEO.instancing, C-GEOLOD, virtualized-geometry-lod, vegetation-foliage
findings.finding: No capability covers instance sharing inside a cluster hierarchy (hierarchical/assembly instancing) or dense masked and thin foliage in the virtualized-geometry tier. vegetation-foliage owns 'vegetation instancing & rendering', geometry-pipeline owns RND.GEO.instancing, virtualized-geometry-lod owns cluster LOD, and C-GEOLOD is optional for vegetation. C-MATIF already carries WPO and mask, so the material half exists but the geometry half has no owner.
findings.evidence: UE 5.5-5.7 Nanite Assemblies and Nanite foliage (voxel foliage LOD, WPO disable distances); open-world foliage is the dominant geometry cost and the case where cluster LOD breaks (alpha test, wind motion, sub-pixel thin geometry).
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.LOD.instanced-clusters (instance sharing, assemblies, per-instance bounds expansion for WPO) and RND.LOD.foliage (masked/thin-geometry LOD, voxel/impostor transition), owner virtualized-geometry-lod, contributors vegetation-foliage and geometry-pipeline. State in vegetation-foliage non-responsibilities that cluster LOD is not its own, and make C-GEOLOD non-optional for vegetation on std3d.

findings.finding: Depth and projection conventions (reverse-Z, float depth, infinite far plane, jitter in clip space, pixel-center and Y-flip differences across D3D/Vulkan/Metal/WebGPU) have no capability. C-SCENETEX lists depth and HZB without convention, and C-MATH conventions are generic. Independent agents writing HZB, VSM, RT, TAA and vendor upscaler integrations will diverge.
findings.evidence: Reversed-Z float depth is the de facto standard (UE, Frostbite, HDRP); DLSS/FSR/XeSS integration guides fix depth, motion-vector and jitter conventions.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.ARCH.depth-convention (owner render-architect, contributors math-simd-numerics, reconstruction-upscaling, xr-runtime), reference it in C-SCENETEX, and add a render-validation conformance case.

findings.finding: No shader numeric-precision policy exists (FP16/RelaxedPrecision/min16, packed math, subgroup-size assumptions). C-MATH precision classes are CPU-side. Half precision is a major ALU and register lever on mobile, portable and console GPUs and a common source of banding and NaN bugs.
findings.evidence: Arm, Qualcomm and Apple GPU best-practice guides; PS5/Xbox packed FP16; DXC 16-bit types and SM 6.2+ native FP16.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.SHADER.precision (mixed-precision policy per tier and pass, FP32-reference validation via render-validation), owner shader-system, contributors platform-mobile and material-system, gated through C-GPUTIER.

findings.finding: Runtime offscreen render products are not owned: isolated render scenes with their own lighting and budget for 3D UI (character creator, inventory previews, portraits, icons), in-world render-to-texture (mirrors, security cameras, minimap), and player capture (photo-mode tiled high-res capture, UI-less and HDR screenshot output, platform share-capture restrictions). multiview mentions 'captures' in passing, preview-world in C-EDVIEW is editor-only, and QA final-frame capture is a test tool.
findings.evidence: Common in shipped games (inventory 3D previews, tiled photo modes with TAA/DoF overrides); console share and protected-content capture rules.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.ARCH.offscreen-scenes and RND.ARCH.capture owned by render-architect, contributors ui-architect, gameplay-camera and platform-services, and add a C-CERT entry for capture restrictions.

findings.finding: Baked PVS/portal-cell visibility is a Quake-era technique carried as an unscoped E capability with no profile tag and no legacy-catalogue justification. Agents may use it on GPU-driven tiers where two-phase HZB culling replaces it.
findings.evidence: Modern use is confined to mobile and CPU-culled paths (Umbra-class occlusion, indoor cell/portal); GPU-driven tiers use HZB culling.
findings.proposed_change: Tag the capability lite3d (CPU-submitted tier) and add a legacy pattern with default stance 'GPU HZB culling; baked visibility only on the CPU-culled tier by ADR' and stance_capabilities [RND.GEO.culling, RND.GEO.cpu-occlusion, RND.GEO.precomputed-visibility].

findings.finding: L29 says 'async creation with fallbacks' but no capability owns the behavior when a PSO is not ready (skip, hold, fallback material, block). The correct choice is pass-dependent (depth and shadow passes, RT hit pipelines before TLAS use, gameplay-critical geometry) and spans rhi-core, shader-system and material-system.
findings.evidence: UE PSO precache skip/delay policies and Unity shader warmup; the hitch versus pop-in tradeoff in vendor PSO-stutter guidance.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.MAT.pso-miss-policy (per-pass and material-domain policy table, telemetry to PRF.LOAD.hitch-gate), owner material-system, contributors rhi-core, shader-system, render-architect; add it to L29 stance_capabilities.

findings.target: render-2d-vector, post-color-hdr, vfx-particles, material-system, C-VT, C-COLOR, C-TEMPORAL, C-SCENETEX, C-RSCENE
findings.finding: In minimal/2D configurations non-optional edges pull the 3D render stack into 2D and UI-only builds: render-2d-vector consumes C-VT and C-COLOR non-optionally, post-color-hdr consumes C-TEMPORAL and C-SCENETEX, vfx-particles (profile all) consumes C-RSCENE, C-MATIF, C-SCENETEX, material-system consumes C-VT. A card game therefore needs virtual texturing, temporal history plumbing and the scene-texture registry, contradicting the batched-draw-list 2D stance.
findings.evidence: model.deps() over minimal-client members. Unity URP 2D, Godot Compatibility and Bevy 2D run without VT/TAA/G-buffer registry.
findings.proposed_change: Make C-VT optional in render-2d-vector/material-system, C-TEMPORAL and C-SCENETEX optional in post-color-hdr, split the 2D-needed part of C-COLOR, retag vfx-particles/reconstruction-upscaling; add check that minimal/min2d closures contain none of C-VT, C-TEMPORAL, C-SCENETEX, C-RSCENE.

findings.target: skills.json profiles/targets, configurations minimal-client and online-3d-server, reference-games
findings.finding: Scale-down is proven only as closure, not minimality. Membership is profile 'all' or match, and most skills are tagged all, so minimal-client (no physics UI/card game) has 74 skills vs 98 for standard-3d-client, including anti-cheat-integrity, cinematics-sequencer, vfx-particles, media-playback, animation-graphs, ai-behavior-perception, reconstruction-upscaling and reference-games. online-3d-server includes cloth-deformables, motion-synthesis, vegetation-foliage, atmosphere-weather, water-ocean, localization-i18n.
findings.evidence: model.members() output; check.py asserts closure only.
findings.proposed_change: Give configurations explicit feature roots and add a reachability check (every member reachable from roots or universals); retag anti-cheat to online add-ons, cinematics/vfx/media/ai/animation-graphs to opt-in profiles, drop server target from cosmetic skills unless a headless capability exists; make reference-games a non-build kind.

findings.target: C-SNAPSHOT, C-REP, C-PREDICT, C-SAVE, C-SRVDATA, C-SIGNIF, CORE.REFL.attributes, CORE.ECS.snapshot
findings.finding: Each stateful subsystem must declare its state independently to snapshot, replication, prediction, save, server persistence and tier hand-off registries; no capability owns a single state-class schema (transient/derived/saved/replicated/predicted/persisted/editor-only) on reflected properties. Features such as GAM.FW.customization-descriptor and GAM.NARR.facts re-declare participation ad hoc, so saved-but-not-predicted or replicated-but-not-snapshotted state cannot be detected.
findings.evidence: contract summaries; Unreal UPROPERTY flags plus separate rollback registration drift; Overwatch ECS talk derives all from one component definition.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.REFL.state-classes (owner reflection-metadata) and contract C-STATECLASS (L2, requires C-REFL) from which C-SNAPSHOT/C-REP/C-PREDICT/C-SAVE/C-SRVDATA derive, plus a fitness function that every declared component/property has a class.

findings.target: PHY.ARCH.validation, ANM.ARCH.validation, AUD.ARCH.validation, GAM.AI.validation, RES.MGMT.validation, UI.FW.validation vs QA.SIM.stability-suite, QA.SIM.animation, QA.SIM.audio
findings.finding: Oracle suites are owned twice: physics/animation/audio 'oracle suite' capabilities belong to the implementing leads while QA.SIM.* own the same metrics and simulation-validation is the declared oracle_author of C-PHYS/C-ANIM/C-AUDIO. GAM.AI.validation and RES.MGMT.validation put suites with implementers while C-NAV/C-RES name another oracle author. Unlike RND.MAT.validation they lack the 'hooks only' qualifier, contradicting the implementer-vs-oracle-author independence rule.
findings.evidence: contracts.json oracle_author; capability texts; ARCH.ORG.independence.
findings.proposed_change: Reword all *.validation capabilities as hooks/reference scenes/threshold proposals with suite authorship by the oracle_author; add QA.SIM.navigation and QA.SIM.streaming (or reassign C-NAV/C-RES oracle authors); add a check that owner-equals-implementer oracle capabilities carry the hooks-only marker.

findings.target: robustness-fuzzing, functional-automation-soak, simulation-validation, render-validation (oracle_author of 111 code contracts)
findings.finding: Four process skills author every conformance suite: functional-automation-soak 35 contracts, robustness-fuzzing 26, simulation-validation 26, render-validation 24. robustness-fuzzing (5 capabilities) is oracle author for C-MATH, C-SYNC, C-TASK, C-MEM, C-ECS, C-CFG, C-CRASH, C-ML; functional-automation-soak for C-TEXT, C-LOC, C-BUILD, C-VCS, C-EDCMD. This breaks the distinct-expertise rule and serializes milestone freezes behind four agents.
findings.evidence: contracts.json oracle_author counts; oracle_reference entries name unrelated literatures (litmus tests, CLDR, Perfetto, ONNX parity).
findings.proposed_change: Add experts foundation-conformance (memory model, math reference, containers, allocator, config, ECS model tests) and ui-text-conformance (shaping, CLDR, layout, focus) under test-architect and re-point the affected contracts; keep robustness-fuzzing for parsers and fault campaigns.

findings.target: ARCH.ORG.ownership-ledger, ARCH.ORG.agent-continuity, ARCH.ORG.write-sets, ARCH.ORG.provenance, BLD.CI.sealed-suites, ARCH.GOV.fitness, program-orchestration, C-ORCH
findings.finding: The coordination machinery is software (lease/lock server with fencing tokens, per-path access-class enforcement incl. sealed:oracle, work queue, provenance store, fitness-function runner) but is owned by process skills, which docs/00 says cannot own code; no tool or runtime skill builds, tests or operates it, and it is labelled emerging.
findings.evidence: ARCH.ORG.agent-continuity text; C-ORCH summary; process-skill-cannot-own-code rationale for security-runtime.
findings.proposed_change: Add a tool-kind expert orchestration-infrastructure owning ledger/lease service, ACL enforcement in VCS/CI, work queue, provenance store and fitness runner; split C-ORCH into a process protocol and a code contract with chaos-test oracle; include it in M0.

findings.target: milestones M1-M3 contracts_frozen; indie-2d-client, minimal-client, fighting-2d-rollback-client; C-RG, C-SHADER, C-MATIF, C-RSCENE, C-DRAW2D, C-COLOR, C-PHYS
findings.finding: M2 claims indie-2d/minimal/fighting-2d shipping on PC, console, mobile and web while the non-optional contracts C-RG, C-SHADER, C-MATIF, C-RSCENE, C-SCENETEX, C-DRAW2D, C-COLOR, C-TEMPORAL, C-VT, C-PHYS are frozen only at M3; shipped games sit on contracts M3 may change. check.py verifies freeze-before-consumer and order, not that a claimed configuration's closure is frozen by the claiming milestone.
findings.evidence: computed from milestones.json and model.deps for M2 claims.
findings.proposed_change: Add a check that every non-optional contract in a claimed configuration's closure is frozen at or before the claim; freeze the 2D-relevant subset in M1/M2 with an extension tier for 3D additions, or move 2D shipping claims to M3.

findings.target: NET.PRED.lagcomp, PHY.ARCH.rewind, ANM.RT.pose-history, GAM.SYS.hit-detection, GAM.SYS.projectiles, anti-cheat-integrity, C-PREDICT
findings.finding: Lag compensation/server rewind is split across four skills (collider history in physics, pose history in animation, window and protocol in prediction-rollback, hurtbox resolution and rewind validation in gameplay toolkit) with no contract naming the composite 'hit volumes with poses as of tick T'; consistency, memory cost per tick and fairness policy are unowned.
findings.evidence: capability texts; C-PREDICT only says 'rewind queries'; Overwatch/Valorant/Source lag compensation treat it as one subsystem.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.PRED.rewound-world-query and contract C-REWIND (L3) with collider-history and pose-history providers implemented by physics and animation-runtime, consumed by C-ABILITY and C-INTEGRITY; oracle author simulation-validation.

findings.target: PHY.ARCH.materials, C-ENV, GAM.SYS.impacts, WLD.ENV.terrain-materials, audio-content-runtime, vfx-particles
findings.finding: The surface-type taxonomy is owned by physics-architect but is the shared key for terrain layers (C-ENV surface type), audio, VFX/decals, projectile penetration and haptics; terrain consumes C-PHYS only optionally and audio/VFX not at all, so consumers cannot legitimately depend on the owner and routing sits in layer-4 GAM.SYS.impacts.
findings.evidence: skills.json consumes for terrain, audio-content-runtime; capability texts.
findings.proposed_change: Move surface-type IDs/hierarchy/parameters to an asset-level owner (gameplay-data or content-pipeline-architect, capability GAM.DATA.surface-types, contract C-SURFACE); keep PHY.ARCH.materials as physics parameter binding and reference shared IDs from C-ENV, audio, VFX, material-system.

findings.finding: Same owner says both that ordering is derived from declared access by one scheduler and that the simulation schedule is a fixed sequence with declared access used only for validation; agents cannot tell whether adding a system may reorder simulation.
findings.evidence: capability texts and C-FRAME summary.
findings.proposed_change: Reword sim-schedule as a fixed relative order of named simulation groups (determinism anchor) with derived ordering inside groups and access-versus-canonical-order violations failing validation; state in C-FRAME.

findings.finding: A runtime skill shipping in client, headless and server builds is parented to the tool lead editor-architect, so a tool lead without runtime literature arbitrates server-shipping code under the intra-subtree arbitration rule.
findings.evidence: skills.json parent/kind/targets; ARCH.ORG.escalation.
findings.proposed_change: Reparent to core-runtime-architect or observability-telemetry with editor hosting via C-EDHOST, or record an arbitration exception in ARCH.ORG.escalation.

findings.finding: engine-architect has 29 direct children and is sole arbiter for intra-workstream, cross-workstream and party-lead disputes with no workstream coordinator; also C-A11Y is the only contract never frozen because check.py requires freezes only for code contracts.
findings.evidence: skills.json parent counts; milestones.json; check.py line 352.
findings.proposed_change: Designate a workstream coordinator (non-party lead) as first-instance arbiter and reserve engine-architect for cross-workstream cases; freeze C-A11Y at M1 and extend the never-frozen check to named process contracts.

findings.target: C-TASK, CORE.JOBS.*, job-system-task-graph, RES.MGMT.pipeline, ED.ARCH.async-jobs, ML.RT.sequence-exec
findings.finding: No capability or C-TASK obligation covers task cancellation (tokens, propagation to dependents, cancelling in-flight IO/GPU work, cancel-vs-completion and cancel-vs-retire ordering). Cancellation appears only as local words in RES.MGMT.pipeline, ED.ARCH.async-jobs and ML.RT.sequence-exec, so three owners will invent different semantics on the async path and race publish against cancel and handle release.
findings.evidence: Structured concurrency and stop tokens (.NET CancellationToken, C++26 std::execution stop_token, Swift task cancellation); io_uring and DirectStorage expose cancel but the completion race must be defined once.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.JOBS.cancellation (owner job-system-task-graph; contributors async-io-storage, resource-streaming-architect, concurrency-primitives); add cancel/stop-token and cancel-vs-completion semantics to the C-TASK summary; the three local capabilities reference it; add a cancellation-race case to C-TASK and C-RES oracle references.

findings.finding: The IO stack is read-only. No owner exists for durable write primitives (write scheduling/coalescing, fsync/F_FULLFSYNC, directory sync, atomic replace, disk-full, write-vs-read deadline arbitration). The only atomic-write capability is GAM.SAVE.atomic at layer 4, unusable by lower consumers. The editor journal, DDC, PSO/shader cache, crash dumps, telemetry spool, server write-behind and cook outputs will each reimplement it or bypass IO arbitration.
findings.evidence: SQLite/LMDB durability docs (macOS needs F_FULLFSYNC); RocksDB WAL practice; Windows FlushFileBuffers semantics; SSD endurance of logging-heavy builds.
findings.proposed_change: Add RES.IO.write (owner async-io-storage; contributors platform-architect, persistence-save) with write queues, durability classes, atomic replace, quota/disk-full errors and read-deadline protection; add to C-IO summary; keep GAM.SAVE.atomic for save-format policy only; add a power-cut crash-consistency oracle to C-IO.

findings.finding: The allocator family lists 'linear/frame' allocators, but the framework has overlapping frames in flight, multi-frame tasks and per-world cadences, so 'frame' is not a lifetime. memory-allocators consumes only C-PAL, C-BASE and C-SYNC, not C-LIFETIME or any completion token, so nothing says scratch arenas reset only when a frame-slot or task-completion token retires. This is the frame-tied lifetime pattern the anti-legacy catalogue rejects.
findings.evidence: Frostbite/Destiny transient-allocator and frame-graph talks; UE FMemStack scoped to task lifetime; per-frame-in-flight ring buffers reset by fence in Vulkan/D3D12.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'scoped arenas: reset keyed to a completion token or frame-in-flight slot (C-LIFETIME)'; add C-LIFETIME to memory-allocators consumes (same layer L1); add 'arena reuse under 3 overlapping frames and a cancelled task' to C-MEM/C-LIFETIME oracle references.

findings.finding: CPU-visible GPU memory rules are unowned: memory-type and coherence policy (write-combined vs cached, host-visible device-local/ReBAR, non-temporal stores, no CPU reads from WC memory, cache maintenance on non-coherent paths). CORE.MEM.uma is accounting only; RND.MEM.upload names rings only.
findings.evidence: AMD GPUOpen Vulkan/D3D12 memory allocation guidance; Apple Metal storage modes; Arm Mali/Adreno cache-maintenance best practices.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.MEM.cpu-visible (owner gpu-memory-resources; contributor memory-allocators) with a per-platform memory-type matrix and a no-CPU-read-from-upload-memory lint; reference from CORE.MEM.uma and the C-GPUMEM summary.

findings.finding: Priority inversion is unaddressed: CORE.CONC.sync specifies futex locks and spin-with-backoff but no priority inheritance/donation, while the framework mixes real-time audio, latency-critical lanes, QoS classes and P/E cores with shared locks. Thread-model has real-time thread rules but no lock rules.
findings.evidence: Mars Pathfinder; Linux PI-futex; Apple os_unfair_lock donation; Bencina 'Real-time audio programming 101'; Android ADPF spin guidance.
findings.proposed_change: Extend CORE.CONC.sync with priority inheritance/donation where the OS offers it, no spinning across QoS classes, and a lock-class registry (frame-critical, RT-forbidden) checked by CORE.CONC.correctness; add an RT-thread forbidden-primitive lint to thread-model.

findings.finding: Only dev-time memory debugging exists; there is no field detection of heap corruption in shipping builds (sampled guard-page allocator, hardware memory tagging). MTE/PAC is a mention inside a security capability marked M and the allocator owner has no obligation to expose it.
findings.evidence: GWP-ASan (Chrome, Android); Arm MTE async mode with Scudo; PartitionAlloc guard pages.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.MEM.field-detection (owner memory-allocators; contributors crash-diagnostics, security-engineering): sampled guard allocator (E) and MTE tag-check mode (M, radar entry), overhead budgets in C-BUDGET, feeding OBS.CRASH.capture bucketing.

findings.finding: False sharing appears only as an after-the-fact analysis capability (PRF.CPU.contention). No design-side owner states destructive-interference size use, padding/alignment rules for cross-thread data, or per-worker sharded counters and queues, so independent agents writing lock-free structures will produce late-found contention.
findings.evidence: LMAX Disruptor padding; Folly/Abseil sharded counters; C++17 hardware_destructive_interference_size; 128-byte lines on Apple silicon.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.CONC.layout (owner concurrency-primitives; contributors containers-core-types, platform-architect): per-target interference size, sharding rules, padding lint; analysis stays with PRF.CPU.contention.

findings.finding: C-CRASH is layer 1 requiring only C-BASE/C-INSTR, yet C-IPC (layer 2) lists the crash handler as an endpoint. No capability owns crash-time safety: async-signal-safe/SEH-safe code, pre-reserved emergency heap, alternate signal stack for stack overflow, out-of-process capture over PAL pipes, and OOM inside the handler. Capture routed through the engine allocator or scheduler fails in OOM and deadlock crashes.
findings.evidence: Crashpad/Breakpad design (out-of-process, no allocation in handler); POSIX async-signal-safe list; Windows stack-overflow SEH constraints.
findings.proposed_change: Add OBS.CRASH.safe-path (owner crash-diagnostics; contributors platform-architect, memory-allocators); state the crash handler uses PAL process/pipe primitives via C-BASE only and is not a C-IPC dependency; fix the C-IPC summary; add crash-in-OOM and crash-with-lock-held cases to C-CRASH conformance.

findings.target: milestones M2/M4; C-REP; C-PREDICT; C-HOSTAUTH; C-NETSESSION
findings.finding: C-REP, C-PREDICT, C-NETSESSION and C-HOSTAUTH are frozen at M2, but no configuration claimed by M2 contains replication; the first configurations with replication, lag compensation, server-authoritative reconciliation, listen and dedicated hosting are claimed at M4. The contracts are frozen before their real consumers exist. check.py only proves that an owner and some consumer skill exist, not that a claimed configuration exercises the contract.
findings.evidence: M2 exit proves only rollback and async play. Interpolation, interest management, RPC authority and lag compensation first appear in the M4 exit. C-SERVER is frozen after M4, so the ladder intends freeze after proof.
findings.proposed_change: Freeze C-REP at M4. Split the C-PREDICT freeze: rollback and lockstep at M2, server-authoritative reconciliation and lag compensation at M4. Or add a server-authoritative configuration to M2. Add a check that a contract is frozen only at a milestone claiming a configuration containing its owner and a consumer.

findings.finding: Session events (join-ready, baseline start, travel, reconnect with ownership restore, disconnect) have no declared direction into replication. replication does not consume C-NETSESSION. net-session consumes C-REP? optionally and not C-SNAPSHOT although baseline is 'replicated snapshot or C-SNAPSHOT + command catch-up'. Only prediction-rollback consumes C-NETSESSION.
findings.evidence: Unreal NetDriver/PlayerController join and seamless travel, Unity Netcode/Mirror connection-ready callbacks, Photon Fusion late-join snapshots all give replication session lifecycle callbacks.
findings.proposed_change: Define a participant interface in C-NETSESSION (on_join_ready, provide_baseline, on_travel, on_reconnect, on_disconnect) implemented by replication, prediction-rollback and determinism-replay. Add C-NETSESSION to replication.consumes and drop C-REP? from net-session.consumes.

findings.finding: NET.SESS.disconnect owns the ban hook and C-HOSTAUTH claims kick/ban in every host mode, but nothing declares the edge from an integrity verdict to enforcement: anti-cheat-integrity does not consume C-HOSTAUTH and net-session does not consume C-INTEGRITY. Only dedicated-server consumes both, so listen, P2P, rollback and lockstep hosts have no path from anomaly signal to kick/ban.
findings.evidence: EOS Anti-Cheat and Steam VAC integrations register kick callbacks with the session layer; server validators act via the connection layer.
findings.proposed_change: net-session consumes C-INTEGRITY? and applies verdicts through C-HOSTAUTH. C-INTEGRITY declares verdict types (kick, ban, quarantine, flag). Add a listen-host kick conformance case.

findings.target: NET.TRANS.crypto; NET.SESS.auth; NET.SESS.handshake; NET.ARCH.versioning; auth-tickets input
findings.finding: Auth-ticket and service-identity validation is stated in two capabilities with different owners (NET.TRANS.crypto and NET.SESS.auth), and the handshake in three (NET.ARCH.versioning, NET.SESS.handshake, the transport crypto handshake). Nothing says where the transport handshake ends and the session handshake begins, or who binds the ticket to the transport session key.
findings.evidence: Ticket replay and unauthenticated-state windows between transport handshake (DTLS/QUIC) and game login are a known failure class in Source/Unreal and EOS/Steam ticket flows.
findings.proposed_change: NET.TRANS.crypto covers only channel encryption and key establishment (remove ticket/service-identity from its text). NET.SESS.auth is sole owner of ticket validation and channel binding. Add an authenticated-channel state with key-binding token to C-NETLINK. NET.ARCH.versioning keeps policy only.

findings.target: dedicated-server purpose; NET.SESS.budgets; NET.SESS.overload; NET.SRV.admin; C-HOSTAUTH; C-SERVER
findings.finding: dedicated-server's purpose still claims overload degradation and per-connection budgets, which are net-session capabilities (NET.SESS.budgets/overload, C-HOSTAUTH). The admin surface is in both C-HOSTAUTH ('host-local admin surface') and C-SERVER/NET.SRV.admin ('authenticated admin command surface'): two contracts, two owners, one RBAC/audit surface, and listen hosts get neither.
findings.evidence: skills.json purpose text versus capabilities.json ownership and contracts.json summaries.
findings.proposed_change: Remove budgets and overload from the dedicated-server purpose. C-HOSTAUTH keeps kick/ban and quota primitives only; NET.SRV.admin owns RBAC, audit and remote transport; listen hosts expose only the local console.

findings.target: configurations; dedicated-server profiles; NET.SESS.host-mode; NET.PRED.spectator; QA.FUNC.network
findings.finding: No configuration has a server or headless target for lockstep or rollback; dedicated-server, replication and server-scaleout carry only the 'online' profile. rts-*, fighting-2d-rollback-* and lockstep tools are client/tools only. Relay-hosted or referee hosting, server-side desync arbitration, server-run input spectators, replay verification and a headless bot for the M2 rollback and M4 2-hour lockstep soak are not proven closed; online-3d-bot-client exists only for std3d.
findings.evidence: Hosted rollback/lockstep relays and spectator servers (League of Legends spectator, Age of Empires relay, GGPO-with-relay titles), tournament referee servers.
findings.proposed_change: Add rts-2d-lockstep-server (min2d, massim, online-lockstep, server) and fighting-2d-rollback-headless-client (min2d, online-rollback, headless-client). Give dedicated-server the online-lockstep and online-rollback profiles or a slim relay/referee variant. Claim them at M2/M4.

findings.target: NET.PRED.lagcomp; NET.REP.interpolation; C-INPUT; C-PREDICT; C-REP; PHY.ARCH.rewind; ANM.RT.pose-history
findings.finding: Lag compensation needs the client view time (interpolation tick pair and delay) at fire time. Replication produces it, C-INPUT frames must carry it, prediction-rollback consumes it, C-PHYS collider history and C-ANIM pose history are queried with it. No contract carries it: C-INPUT is only tick-stamped command frames, C-PREDICT no longer requires C-REP, and the composed rewound query is split across three contracts with no owner. No rewind-window/memory budget line exists.
findings.evidence: Valve Source Multiplayer Networking (usercmd view interp fields), Overwatch GDC 2017 server rewind window, Unreal networked-physics lag comp.
findings.proposed_change: Add an extensible view-stamp field to C-INPUT command frames. C-REP exposes client view time. Add a C-PREDICT rewound-query facade composing C-PHYS and C-ANIM histories. Add a rewind window and memory line to C-BUDGET per configuration.

findings.finding: Host migration is a clause inside NET.SESS.host-mode with contributors network-architect and dedicated-server only. It needs replicated state or snapshot, prediction state and authority transfer (replication, determinism-replay, prediction-rollback, distributed-authority) and has no oracle scenario.
findings.evidence: Halo Reach / Destiny P2P host migration post-mortems; Photon/Unreal host migration requires authoritative object hand-off.
findings.proposed_change: Split out NET.SESS.host-migration owned by net-session with contributors replication, prediction-rollback, determinism-replay; add a host-drop scenario to NET.ARCH.validation and QA.SIM.netsim.

findings.finding: NET.ARCH.budgets (network-architect) and C-BUDGET (performance-architect) both hold budget numbers, but C-BUDGET names no network line (per-connection bytes/s, server egress per CCU, tick cost per player, packet rate) and there are no named link-condition profiles (home Wi-Fi, cellular, console NAT, long-haul) shared by NET.TRANS.simulation, QA.SIM.netsim and PRF.NET.*.
findings.evidence: Unreal/Unity network emulation presets; Valorant netcode per-tier bandwidth targets.
findings.proposed_change: Add network lines and named link-class profiles to C-BUDGET, with values supplied by NET.ARCH.budgets; QA and PRF read the stored table.

findings.finding: LAN discovery replies, master-server responses and community server-list entries (names, endpoints, content URLs) are pre-auth hostile-remote data rendered in UI and used to choose connect addresses, but are not registered (packets covers frames, service-responses covers backends).
findings.evidence: Quake-family master server and Source A2S query abuse; server-name injection into UI.
findings.proposed_change: Register server-list-entries: validating owner net-session, parser network-transport, limits length/count/rate and endpoint allow-list, with a fuzz target.

findings.finding: ANM.RT.pose-history is restricted to lite3d/std3d, but min2d online configurations contain prediction-rollback with lag compensation; animated 2D hitboxes (skeletal 2D, frame-data sprites) have no history owner.
findings.evidence: 2D skeletal shooters with server rewind need hitbox history (Spine/DragonBones-driven hitboxes).
findings.proposed_change: Add min2d to the capability profiles or add a 2D hitbox-history obligation in physics-2d via PHY.ARCH.rewind.

findings.target: PHY.2D.*, physics-2d, collision-detection, rigid-body-dynamics, PHY.COL.queries/filtering/ccd, PHY.DYN.joints/islands/kinematic, PHY.CTRL.platforms/sensing; configs indie-2d-client, sandbox-2d-client, fighting-2d-rollback-client
findings.finding: In every min2d configuration, queries, filtering/layers, CCD, joints, sleeping, kinematic bodies and platform riding are absent from the closure, because collision-detection and rigid-body-dynamics are lite3d/std3d only. physics-2d owns only dynamics, controllers, determinism, shape-gen and cellular. No capability covers tilemap colliders (composite/merged, one-way, slopes, runtime tile edits), 2D runtime collider regeneration for destructible terrain, 2D sensors/triggers or 2D ropes/joints. PHY.2D.shape-gen covers sprites only.
findings.evidence: Box2D v3 and Rapier2D ship queries, joints, sensors, CCD and one-way platforms as core. Tilemap collision merging is the dominant 2D collision source (Unity CompositeCollider2D, Godot TileSet physics layers).
findings.proposed_change: Add physics-2d capabilities PHY.2D.queries-filtering, PHY.2D.joints-ropes, PHY.2D.ccd-sensors, PHY.2D.tilemap-collision and PHY.2D.runtime-build (contributors terrain, destruction-fracture, render-2d-vector). Rename PHY.2D.dynamics to state its scope.

findings.finding: character-movement consumes only C-PHYS, whose summary has no controller primitive. Collide-and-slide, step/slope/ledge, up-vector, platform carry and push-vs-dynamic-body are owned by character-physics, which provides no contract. The resimulatable move API needs a controller that can be re-stepped from a snapshot with a per-move step independent of the world step. This is unstated, so no conformance suite can be written.
findings.evidence: Unreal CMC vs Mover; Jolt CharacterVirtual and PhysX CCT. Rollback movement needs snapshotable controller state and query-based moves.
findings.proposed_change: Add contract C-CHARCTRL (layer 3, owner character-physics, requires C-PHYS, oracle_author simulation-validation, conformance: resimulate N moves from a snapshot reproduces state). C-MOVE requires it. Middleware backends implement it through PHY.ARCH.middleware-layer.

findings.finding: Networked physics is one E capability. Predicted general rigid-body rollback with partial island resimulation is not established: PhysX and Jolt do not restore solver warm-start caches or partial islands, Chaos network-physics prediction is beta/experimental, and Rocket League is a bespoke Bullet fork. Established approaches are server-authoritative snapshot interpolation, deterministic lockstep, and rollback of characters and a few vehicles. C-PHYS conformance (restore + resimulate reproduces the hash) is asserted for any backend.
findings.evidence: Rocket League GDC 2018 'It IS Rocket Science'; Fiedler 'Networked Physics'; Unreal Network Physics (5.4/5.5 experimental); Jolt SaveState is full-state only.
findings.proposed_change: Split NET.PRED.physics into (a) server-auth replicated dynamic bodies with interpolation/extrapolation and smoothing (E), (b) predicted physics with rollback and partial resim (M, radar entry falling back to (a)), (c) deterministic lockstep physics (E, only for backends declaring the deterministic level). Split PHY.ARCH.rewind into full snapshot/hash/collider history (E) and partial-island resim (M). Restrict the C-PHYS conformance clause to the declared level.

findings.finding: Nothing turns the physics active set into replicated state. replication consumes C-ECS/C-SPATIAL, not C-PHYS, and contracts are ECS-independent by principle. Physics-body replication needs sleep flags, quantized pose/velocity, significance-based priority, prop extrapolation, prop and vehicle ownership hand-off, and debris bandwidth budgets. The only home is NET.PRED.physics, a prediction skill whose boundary excludes the physics solver.
findings.evidence: Fiedler/Rocket League state compression, Halo Reach, Unreal Iris physics replication, Sea of Thieves ship replication.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.REP.physics-bodies (owner replication, contributors physics-architect, prediction-rollback). Add optional C-PHYS to replication.consumes, with C-PHYS exposing an active-set/change-set output. Route prop and vehicle authority hand-off through NET.ARCH.distributed-authority using it.

findings.target: profiles of cloth-deformables, destruction-fracture, fluid-simulation; configs lite-3d-*, xr-standalone-client, online-3d-server, rts-2d-massim-client, sandbox-2d-client
findings.finding: Profile membership is skill-wide. Every lite3d build (mobile, portable, XR standalone) closes over cloth-deformables and destruction-fracture. Every server config includes cloth-deformables, although cloth/hair are cosmetic. 2D massim and sandbox configs pull 3D fluid-simulation via the massim/sandbox tags while their cellular fluid capability is owned by physics-2d.
findings.evidence: Mobile 3D uses bone-chain secondary motion, and the radar already names bone-chain dynamics as the hair fallback. Dedicated servers strip cosmetic simulation (Fortnite, Overwatch).
findings.proposed_change: Drop lite3d from cloth-deformables and destruction-fracture and gate them on a new addon (e.g. physfx). Add capability-level client-only tags for cosmetic cloth, hair and softbody, while ropes and structural destruction stay available on servers. Restrict fluid-simulation to aaa and sandbox-3d. Point the lite3d fallback at ANM secondary-motion springs.

findings.finding: The lead owns 22 capabilities against 9 to 11 for the experts. About half are implementation of the shared physics-world runtime (handles, event pipeline, streaming insertion, dehydrate/rehydrate, capture, force fields, middleware adapter, fixed-point and GPU backends). The lead is decider, implementer and middleware patch owner, a single-agent bottleneck contradicting 'few orchestrators, many focused experts'. PHY.ARCH.events also overlaps contact generation done in collision-detection and rigid-body-dynamics.
findings.evidence: Physics stacks separate architecture policy from the integration/runtime layer (UE Chaos core vs integration, Jolt/PhysX adapters).
findings.proposed_change: Add expert physics-runtime-integration (parent physics-architect, workstream simulation) owning world, events, streaming, persistence, rewind mechanics, multi-world, debug-capture, fields, materials, middleware-layer, fixed-point-backend, gpu, async, lwc. The lead keeps build-integrate, determinism, lod, stepping policy, local-frames, tier-transitions, learned-surrogates and validation.

findings.finding: The actuator registry has no simulation actuators (substeps/solver iterations, active-body cap, CCD/query budgets, cloth/fluid particle counts, mass-agent counts). No policy bounds fixed-step catch-up (max substeps, dilation vs drop, the accumulator spiral of death). Only NET.SESS.overload registers server actuators, so the governor cannot shed simulation load on mobile or portable tiers.
findings.evidence: Fiedler 'Fix Your Timestep'; Box2D and Jolt expose iteration and substep knobs; console titles cap substeps and dilate time.
findings.proposed_change: Add PHY.ARCH.budget-degradation (owner physics-architect) and register its actuators in CORE.SCALE.actuators. Add a bounded-catch-up/overrun policy to CORE.FRAME.fixed-step, keeping cadence fixed for lockstep. Crowd and systems-simulation register their own actuators.

findings.target: CORE.FRAME.sim-schedule, CORE.FRAME.phases, CORE.FRAME.access-model, docs/00 line 90, ANM.ARCH.sync
findings.finding: sim-schedule says 'fixed sequence; declared access used only for validation', while phases, access-model and the principles say ordering is derived from declared access. The two regimes are not reconciled. Contributors omit ik-procedural-animation, cloth-deformables, vehicle-physics, destruction-fracture, crowd-simulation, ai-behavior-perception and gameplay-systems-toolkit. The split physics/animation/gameplay coupling is not defined: pre-physics animation and kinematic bodies, step, post-physics IK/ragdoll/cloth/hit queries, gameplay reaction. That split is where one-frame-lag bugs in physics-animation-gameplay coupling originate.
findings.evidence: Unreal tick groups (PrePhysics/PostPhysics); Naughty Dog GDC 'Parallelizing the Naughty Dog Engine'; Overwatch ECS GDC 2017.
findings.proposed_change: State in sim-schedule and principle 00 that the simulation sub-schedule is a fixed deterministic order and all other work is derived from access declarations. Add the missing contributors. Define named simulation slots (pre-physics animation, physics step, post-physics animation/cloth, gameplay reaction, replication extract) as a checked artifact.

findings.target: PHY.FLUID.gpu (E), PHY.FLUID.particles (M), PHY.FLUID.grid (M), radar 'Particle & GPU fluids'
findings.finding: GPU fluid solvers are E while the particle and grid fluids they run are M. The radar entry is titled 'Particle & GPU fluids' but lists only particles and grid, so PHY.FLUID.gpu has no fallback or revisit trigger.
findings.evidence: Radar cites Niagara Fluids (beta) and Flex titles only.
findings.proposed_change: Set PHY.FLUID.gpu to M and list it on the radar entry, or merge it into particles/grid.

findings.target: PHY.2D.cellular, GAM.SIM.fields, PHY.FLUID.grid, systems-simulation non_responsibilities, voxel-worlds
findings.finding: physics-2d (falling sand, liquid/gas/heat grids), systems-simulation (diffusion, cellular spread) and fluid-simulation (grid smoke and fire) overlap. systems-simulation's non-responsibility 'Cellular fluids' points to fluid-simulation, but the capability is owned by physics-2d. 3D voxel cellular liquids and smoke (Minecraft-style flow, Space Engineers) have no owner, since physics-2d is min2d only and sandbox-online-server lacks PHY.2D.cellular.
findings.evidence: Noita falling-sand engine (GDC 2019); Minecraft fluid rules; Teardown voxel smoke and debris.
findings.proposed_change: Give deterministic discrete grid/cellular simulation one owner (systems-simulation, 2D and 3D voxel) and move PHY.2D.cellular there. fluid-simulation keeps continuum and particle solvers. Correct the non-responsibility wording in systems-simulation and physics-2d.

findings.finding: No untrusted input covers collision and simulation data from mods and UGC. Runtime collision generation from UGC meshes and cooked collision blobs (BVH, hulls, heightfields, fracture/cloth assets) are consumed by servers and peers. Generic assets limits (size/depth/count) do not bound geometric validity or cook time. Degenerate geometry can spin GJK/EPA, cooking or decomposition, or produce huge hulls and contact counts, a DoS on an authoritative server.
findings.evidence: PhysX and Bullet cooked-data and mesh-parsing CVEs; middleware add hull vertex/triangle limits and validation for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: Add untrusted-input 'physics-assets' (validating_owner collision-detection or physics-architect, parser_owners package-formats-vfs, trust hostile-remote, mode harness, limits on hull vertices, triangles, cook time, body/constraint counts). Require UGC collision cooking to be async, budgeted and sandboxed, and add a fuzz target for cooked-collision deserialization.

findings.finding: No capability owns simulation worst-case cost. QA.SIM.stability-suite measures penetration and energy drift, not step cost. PRF.BENCH.scale-content is generic synthetic worlds, and PRF.NET.resim-cost covers only resim. Contact storms, pile-ups, explosion-to-debris bursts, query storms and mass-agent spikes are the tail cases that break fixed-step budgets.
findings.evidence: Physics hitches are dominated by island wake-ups and CCD bursts; Jolt and Box2D publish worst-case benchmark scenes.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.BENCH.sim-worst-case (owner perf-benchmarking, contributors physics-architect, crowd-simulation, destruction-fracture) and per-tier simulation step budgets in PRF.METH.budgets, tied to PHY.ARCH.budget-degradation.

findings.target: data/legacy-patterns.json (only L30 and L36 touch physics and simulation)
findings.finding: Missing legacy patterns: discrete-only collision patched with speed caps and thick walls; an always-awake single global physics world with no sleeping, active set or simulation LOD; rollback or lockstep over a backend that cannot restore its solver caches; synchronous per-caller scene queries from AI, audio and gameplay (L36 names only mid-step mutation).
findings.evidence: Common in early Unity/Unreal-era projects. PHY.COL.ccd, PHY.DYN.islands, PHY.ARCH.lod and PHY.ARCH.rewind already carry the stances.
findings.proposed_change: Add L75 'Discrete-only collision with speed clamps' (PHY.COL.ccd), L76 'Unbounded always-awake physics world' (PHY.DYN.islands, PHY.ARCH.lod, PHY.ARCH.tier-transitions), L77 'Rollback over non-restorable physics state' (PHY.ARCH.rewind, NET.PRED.sync-test), justification_owner physics-architect.

findings.finding: The external-work arbiter registers streaming, decompression, scene deltas, AS builds and VT pages, but not GPU simulation producers (fluids, cloth, physics offload, crowd VAT). No rule states when gameplay-relevant GPU simulation results are read back or how async readback stays deterministic. Fluid and cloth consume C-RG optionally, so their async-compute placement and byte budgets are unowned.
findings.evidence: PhysX GPU rigid bodies and Flex pipelines; async readback latency of 2 to 3 frames on explicit APIs.
findings.proposed_change: Register GPU simulation as external-work producers with priority, deadline and readback policy. State in PHY.ARCH.gpu that gameplay-visible GPU results are tick-stamped, latched and excluded from deterministic state.

findings.target: C-TARGETPLAT, platform-architect, platform-desktop, platform-console, platform-mobile, platform-web, platform-server-host, PLAT.CON.devkit, PLAT.PAL.devlink
findings.finding: C-TARGETPLAT is a needs_implementer contract (cook format variants, shader backend hook, packager, deploy/launch/debug), but no capability names its content. Only PLAT.CON.devkit and PLAT.PAL.devlink relate to it. Android/iOS device deploy and debug, web dev-server and hosting, and per-platform cook-format selection are unowned rows. Console shader offline compilers appear nowhere (RND.SHADER.toolchain lists DXC, Slang, SPIR-V and Metal only).
findings.evidence: platform-desktop, -mobile, -web and -server-host list C-TARGETPLAT in implements but own no tool-side capability, so the per-target_platform closure proof passes with an empty implementation. Unreal platform extension/cooker/deploy modules and Unity platform build targets are separate first-class work items.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.PAL.target-tools (E, platform-architect) and per-platform rows PLAT.DESK/MOB/WEB/SRV/CON.target-tools covering cook variants, shader-target hook, packager hook and deploy/run/debug. Assign console shader compilers to PLAT.CON with rhi-console as contributor.

findings.target: platform-services, PLAT.SVC.identity, PLAT.SVC.achievements, PLAT.SVC.entitlements, PLAT.SVC.privileges, PLAT.SVC.social, PLAT.SVC.leaderboards, C-SVC, PLAT.CON.confidential-slots
findings.finding: Doc 00 justifies platform-services as 'NDA SDKs plus certification', yet the skill has no access class and no platform tag. Console first-party SDK implementations (trophies, privileges and parental controls, entitlements, presence, activities) live in a non-NDA skill. platform-console implements only the C-SVC user-model slot, and check.py confines NDA skills to platform-console and rhi-console, so the leak is invisible.
findings.evidence: Console platform-holder NDAs bar SDK material from unlicensed parties. Agents are staffed per skill, so one platform-services agent would need every holder's documentation.
findings.proposed_change: Move console-specific PLAT.SVC implementations into holder-partitioned rows (PLAT.CON.svc-*, access nda:per-platform-holder, owner platform-console) behind the public C-SVC interface. Keep platform-services owning the interface, PC/mobile stores and the emulator.

findings.target: BLD.REL.packaging, BLD.REL.submission, BLD.REL.patching, BLD.CI.device-lanes, BLD.CI.build-distribution, QA.CERT.prechecks, PLAT.CON.confidential-slots, packaging-release-patching, ci-cd-automation
findings.finding: Console packaging and signing tools, submission validators, mandated patch/DLC formats and size rules, devkit CI lanes and pre-submission checkers are NDA material. They are owned by non-NDA skills. PLAT.CON.confidential-slots lists runtime slots only and has no packaging, submission, patch-format or devkit-CI slot.
findings.evidence: Console package generators, signing and submission validation ship only in licensed SDKs. C-CERT already partitions requirement text per holder, but no equivalent exists for tool-side material.
findings.proposed_change: Add confidential slots PLAT.CON.packaging, PLAT.CON.submission, PLAT.CON.patch-format and PLAT.CON.ci-lane (owner platform-console, contributors packaging-release-patching and ci-cd-automation), with public stubs on BLD.REL.packaging and BLD.REL.submission.

findings.target: platform_variants.xr-standalone, xr-standalone-client, tools configurations target_platforms, xr-runtime, QA.CERT.programs
findings.finding: No tools configuration lists xr-standalone in target_platforms, so cook, deploy and preview for standalone XR are never proven closed. xr-standalone variants are android-xr and visionos only. Meta Horizon OS/Quest and PICO, with their own store, platform SDK (identity, IAP), OpenXR vendor extensions and store technical requirements, are absent.
findings.evidence: Quest is an Android-derived OS with its own store and mandatory requirements, distinct from Android XR. QA.CERT.programs names only Steam Deck Verified and generic store review. Docs mention Quest only as content.
findings.proposed_change: Add horizon-os and pico-os variants or a recorded non-goal with a revisit trigger. Add an xr-standalone-tools configuration (lite3d+xr, tools, target_platforms [xr-standalone]) claimed in M5. Add headset store programs to QA.CERT.programs.

findings.target: configurations lite-3d-mobile-client, lite-3d-mobile-online-client, lite-3d-portable-console-client, profile lite3d, openworld, PLAT.WEB.webgpu-target, rhi-webgpu
findings.finding: No configuration combines lite3d with openworld, so streaming, world partition and memory arbitration under mobile process-kill limits or portable-console memory are never proven closed. PLAT.WEB.webgpu-target (3D on web, M) and rhi-webgpu are only exercised by 2D web configurations; there is no lite3d@web configuration.
findings.evidence: Mobile and portable open-world titles are among the most shipped and highest-grossing 3D genres and the hardest memory-budget case. Gap analysis A9 flags mobile GPU-driven rendering as thin evidence, but no configuration tests it.
findings.proposed_change: Add lite-3d-mobile-openworld-online-client (lite3d+openworld+online, mobile), lite-3d-portable-openworld-client (lite3d+openworld, console) and lite-3d-web-client (lite3d, web), each claimed in M4 or M5.

findings.target: PLAT.SVC.*, platform-services, QA.CERT.store-policy, platform_variants.pc, BLD.REL.packaging, ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix
findings.finding: The platform matrix promises 'OS x ISA x API x store', but platform_variants has no store axis. No capability owns PC storefront SDK adapters (Steamworks, Epic Online Services, GOG Galaxy, Microsoft Store/GDK-PC), per-store build variants and depots, or Steam Input and overlay rules. platform-services is defined as first-party only.
findings.evidence: Most indie and PC AAA titles ship multi-store SKUs with differing identity, entitlement, achievement, overlay and packaging rules (Steam depots, MSIX, Epic BuildPatchTool). Steam appears in the data only as a transport and Deck-Verified mention.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.SVC.pc-storefronts (E, platform-services, contributors platform-desktop and packaging-release-patching) and BLD.REL.store-variants. Add a store field to configurations or platform_variants.

findings.finding: platform_variants defines variants for pc, mobile, xr-standalone and server-host only. Console holder families and browser engines are absent, so the generated matrix cannot express fixed vs portable console classes or per-browser WebGPU differences.
findings.evidence: platform-console already says 'one agent per platform-holder family' but the families are enumerated nowhere in data.
findings.proposed_change: Add console family variants (anonymized ids acceptable) and web browser variants (chromium, webkit, gecko) to platform_variants, referenced from rhi-console and platform-web variants.

findings.target: UI.A11Y.screen-reader, UI.TXT.ime, ARCH.STRUCT.platform-backends, platform-desktop, platform-mobile, platform-web
findings.finding: The backend-slot registry names an IME/a11y bridge, but only console has a named owner. For desktop, mobile and web the OS accessibility bridges (UIA, NSAccessibility, AT-SPI, UIAccessibility/TalkBack, and the ARIA/DOM shadow tree canvas apps need) sit in accessibility and text-fonts with platform-architect as a contributor. Platform implementers are not on the rows.
findings.evidence: Each bridge is a distinct OS API with its own lifecycle and threading rules. Web canvas content is inaccessible without a DOM mirror. EAA/CVAA compliance (QA.CERT.a11y-law) depends on it.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.DESK/MOB/WEB.a11y-ime-bridge rows (owner platform skill, contributors accessibility and text-fonts), or state explicitly that accessibility owns all non-console OS bridges.

findings.finding: platform-server-host is defined as 'no display or GPU'. Headless GPU hosts (Linux GPU nodes without a display, running offscreen render, GPU bake or texture encode, GPU cook, path-traced reference validation and cloud rendering) have no platform description, and rhi-vulkan does not declare server-host.
findings.evidence: QA.RENDER.reference-validation, QA.RENDER.matrix, the cloud-cook cost ledger and PLAT.PAL.cloud-hybrid all imply GPU compute without a display.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.SRV.headless-gpu (offscreen/headless surfaces, container GPU passthrough, driver pinning) and let rhi-vulkan declare server-host behind a headless flag.

findings.finding: ML.RT.npu (NPU backends via platform ML APIs) is marked X although platform NPU paths (Core ML/Neural Engine, Windows ML/DirectML on Copilot+ PCs, Android accelerator APIs) ship, while ML.RT.os-models is M. C-ML has no platform implementer slot, so per-OS accelerator backends have no platform owner.
findings.evidence: Platform vendors ship these APIs in production. The uncertainty is in-frame scheduling, not API availability.
findings.proposed_change: Split into ML.RT.npu-backends (M, contributors platform-desktop and platform-mobile) and keep in-frame NPU scheduling as X. Add accelerator discovery to PLAT.PAL.capability-tiers.

findings.target: C-EDHOST, C-EDVIEW, ED.WORLD.preview-scenes, ED.UI.asset-editor-host; material-system, animation-runtime, animation-graphs, facial-animation, character-rendering, vfx-particles, cloth-deformables, motion-synthesis, cinematics-sequencer, ik-procedural-animation, virtualized-geometry-lod, vehicle-physics
findings.finding: Preview-world creation is exposed via C-EDVIEW, but asset editors are told to embed preview worlds through C-EDHOST, which requires only C-EDCMD. editor-ui-framework cannot consume C-EDVIEW (world-editor-viewport consumes C-EDHOST, so it would be a cycle) and the ~14 skills with previewing asset editors hold only C-EDCMD/C-EDHOST tool_consumes. check.py demands C-EDVIEW only for world tools, so nothing catches it. Asset editors have no legal path to a preview world, orbit camera, picking or gizmos.
findings.evidence: skills.json tool_consumes; contracts.json C-EDHOST/C-EDVIEW summaries. Unreal FAdvancedPreviewScene/SEditorViewport and Unity PreviewRenderUtility sit below both level editor and asset-editor toolkit.
findings.proposed_change: Add L5 contract C-EDPREVIEW (preview world lifetime, orbit viewport widget, picking, basic gizmos) owned by world-editor-viewport requiring only C-EDCMD; C-EDHOST embeds its panels; add to tool_consumes of every skill with a previewing asset editor; add a check that skills owning spatial-asset editors reach C-EDPREVIEW or C-EDVIEW.

findings.finding: No contract mentions import. asset-import-interchange provides nothing and all CNT.IMP.* have empty contributors, yet one FBX/glTF/USD file yields assets owned by animation, material, physics, LOD and audio skills. Nothing defines importer registration, per-asset-type import-settings schema, domain asset-factory hook, reimport preserving overrides, headless batch import, or the versioned interchange schema external DCC plugins target. The format-owner-owns-builder pattern is inverted: one agent owns import for every domain format. The skill also lacks C-EDHOST/C-EDCMD/C-VCS for import UI, undo and checkout.
findings.evidence: Unreal UFactory/reimport handlers, Unity ScriptedImporter with per-asset settings, Godot EditorImportPlugin: domain teams own importers behind a registered contract.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-IMPORT (L5, owner asset-import-interchange, requires C-ASSET, C-SER, C-COOK, independent oracle author, fuzz target on interchange schema) covering importer registration, import-settings schema, asset-factory hook, reimport-preserve rules, batch entry and schema version. Make animation-runtime, material-system, audio-content-runtime, virtualized-geometry-lod, physics-tools and localization contributors of the relevant CNT.IMP.* capabilities; add C-EDHOST/C-EDCMD/C-VCS to asset-import-interchange tool_consumes.

findings.target: milestones M0-M3 (contracts_draft/frozen); C-EDCMD, C-EDHOST, C-EDVIEW, C-GRAPH, C-VCS; M0/M1 skills owning *.TOOL capabilities
findings.finding: Tool contracts are drafted at M2 and frozen at M3, but skills owning the tool halves of domains arrive earlier (M0: material-system, post-color-hdr, render-2d-vector, texture-streaming-vt, input-system; M1: animation-graphs, animation-runtime, cinematics-sequencer, ui-architect, gameplay-data, ai-behavior-perception, scripting-runtime, localization-i18n, world-data-model). Their tool_consumes reference contracts that do not yet exist. Milestone closure covers only claimed configurations, and M0/M1 claim client targets only, so ~40 skills' tool halves are unproven and the M1 reference games are authored with no editor. Domain formats are fixed before the editability contract (undo granularity, diffable layout, override model) that constrains them.
findings.evidence: milestones.json M0-M3 contracts_draft/frozen and skills lists; skills.json tool_consumes. Unreal's transaction/property systems were retrofitted onto serialization and still constrain formats.
findings.proposed_change: Draft C-EDCMD/C-EDHOST/C-GRAPH/C-VCS at M0 (skeleton includes reflection-driven inspector, command journal, headless commandlet over C-CMD), freeze C-EDCMD/C-EDHOST at M1, move a minimal editor-architect/editor-ui-framework to M1 with a minimal tools configuration claimed at M1, and add a check that a skill owning *.TOOL capabilities is not scheduled before its tool_consumes contracts are drafted.

findings.target: RND.GI.bake-pipeline, WLD.PART.hlod, PHY.TOOL.fluids, AUD.TOOL.acoustics, GAM.AI.navmesh vs CNT.COOK.world-build, CNT.COOK.distributed
findings.finding: Global-illumination 'incremental/distributed bake orchestration' and world-architect 'HLOD generation orchestration' restate the region invalidation, distributed bake and staleness graph owned by CNT.COOK.world-build; fluid, acoustics and navmesh bakes have no stated hookup. Each domain will build its own scheduler, cache keys and staleness UI.
findings.evidence: docs/00 section 4 pattern 'format owner vs pipeline host'; Unreal World Partition builders and Unity's lightmapper had separate bake queues later unified under one build graph.
findings.proposed_change: Reword RND.GI.bake-pipeline and WLD.PART.hlod to builder implementations as C-COOK world-scope processors; orchestration, invalidation, distribution and staleness belong to CNT.COOK.world-build; make fluid, acoustics, navmesh owners contributors of world-build.

findings.target: minimal-tools, indie-2d-tools, fighting-2d-rollback-tools; world-editor-viewport, graph-editor-framework, collaboration-version-control, editor-architect
findings.finding: No tools configuration exists without the editor. minimal-tools (no world) still includes world-editor-viewport, graph-editor-framework and collaboration-version-control because they are profile 'all'; there is no code-first/CLI-only configuration (cook, build, validate via commandlets, text assets). Tool scale-down is proved only as closed, not as editor-optional.
findings.evidence: minimal-tools has 10 tool skills incl. all editor skills; ED.ARCH.headless exists but no configuration proves it stands alone.
findings.proposed_change: Add configuration minimal-cli-tools (target tools, without editor-architect, editor-ui-framework, world-editor-viewport, graph-editor-framework, collaboration-version-control) closed over C-COOK/C-BUILD/C-PKG/C-AUTOMATION, claimed at M1; retag world-editor-viewport to exclude 'minimal'.

findings.finding: CNT.COOK.shared-cache is gated by base profiles lite3d/std3d instead of team size, so a 30-person 2D studio (min2d+team-mid) gets no shared DDC while a solo 3D developer is assigned team/cloud DDC deployment. Team scale is meant to be a separate axis.
findings.evidence: capabilities.json profile tags; docs/00 section 5.
findings.proposed_change: Retag CNT.COOK.shared-cache to team-mid/team-large, keep local DDC in all profiles, and add a check that team-size-named capabilities never carry only base-profile tags.

findings.finding: The rendering workstream is exempt from the authoring-path check and direct lighting has no authoring capability: RND.TOOL.lighting covers probes, captures, scenarios only. Light placement/units, IES/cookies, light functions, shadow-budget and light-complexity views have no owner.
findings.evidence: Unreal light/shader complexity viewmodes and Unity light explorer are standard editor features.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.TOOL.direct-lights owned by direct-lighting-shadows (contributors world-editor-viewport, global-illumination) and add 'rendering' to AUTHORING_WORKSTREAMS.

findings.target: persistence-save and platform-web authoring notes; ED.DEBUG.inspector; GAM.SAVE.*
findings.finding: persistence-save's exemption says save inspection is via visual-debugging-tools, but no capability there covers save inspect/edit/diff/migration dry-run. platform-web's exemption says web preview is the standard editor play mode, but native PIE cannot expose WASM, WebGPU-limit, memory-cap or threading failures.
findings.evidence: skills.json authoring notes versus capability list; QA.FUNC.compat-corpus has no designer/QA tool.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.TOOL.save-inspector owned by persistence-save (inspect/edit/diff/upgrade dry-run over C-SAVE and CORE.SER.evolution); change platform-web's note to C-TARGETPLAT deploy-to-browser plus a web tier in RND.TOOL.scalability-preview.

findings.finding: No capability owns the editor surfaces of configuration and workspace: schema-driven project-settings editor over layered per-platform C-CFG, editor preferences, layout persistence, keybindings, command palette. ED.UI.toolkit covers docking/panels only, so each domain tool will invent its own settings panel.
findings.evidence: No project-settings, shortcut, keybinding, command-palette or workspace capability in ED.*; Unreal Project Settings/Editor Preferences, Unity Shortcut Manager, Godot Project/Editor Settings are shared editor services.
findings.proposed_change: Add ED.UI.settings-editor (reflection-driven over C-CFG, per-platform layers, diff/validate) and ED.UI.workspace (layouts, keybindings, command palette, preferences) to editor-ui-framework; domain tools register commands and settings through C-EDHOST.

findings.target: untrusted-inputs.json; GAM.DATA.spreadsheets, ED.UI.tabular, UI.TOOL.localization, GAM.TOOL.dialogue, ED.COLLAB.codev, ED.COLLAB.production-tracking
findings.finding: Tool-side parsers of vendor/partner files are unregistered: XLSX/CSV round-trip (zip bombs, XXE, formula injection), localization exchange (XLIFF/PO), screenplay imports, audio-middleware imports, vendor delivery packages, tracker webhooks. imported-dcc-files covers DCC geometry only, so check.py cannot force fuzz targets or limits for them.
findings.evidence: untrusted-inputs.json ids versus capabilities naming external file sources.
findings.proposed_change: Add inputs tabular-imports, localization-exchange, narrative-imports, vendor-deliveries, tracker-webhooks with parser owner, fuzz target and size/depth limits.

findings.finding: world-editor-viewport spans three literatures (3D manipulation UX, large-world editing, mesh editing) and provides C-EDVIEW on which ~25 domain tools depend, so modeling/paint work shares the contract's change queue. Separately, ED.COLLAB.binaries (large binary storage) sits in ci-cd-automation while VCS choice, locking and sparse workspaces sit in collaboration-version-control, though depot layout cannot be decided apart from binary storage.
findings.evidence: skills.json expertise fields; docs/00 section 1 split rule.
findings.proposed_change: Move ED.WORLD.blockout and ED.WORLD.mesh-paint to a mesh-editing expert (or asset-cook-processors alongside CNT.COOK.geometry-ops); move ED.COLLAB.binaries to collaboration-version-control with ci-cd-automation as contributor.

findings.target: PRF.CPU.compiler, BLD.SYS.toolchains, BLD.SYS.configs, XC.DET.float, XC.DET.conformance, cpu-performance
findings.finding: Three skills claim compiler flags. PRF.CPU.compiler is 'optimization flag policy (sole owner)' but sits in a process skill that owns no build files. BLD.SYS owns the toolchain matrix and configs, and XC.DET.float owns flags and FMA. PGO/LTO/fast-math change FP results, so a performance flag policy can silently break lockstep, rollback and replay determinism. The XC.DET.conformance matrix omits optimization level, PGO and LTO, so it can pass on dev flags and fail on shipped flags.
findings.evidence: -ffp-contract, /fp:fast and LTO vectorization changing reduction order are known drift sources. Lockstep and rollback titles pin per-module flags for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: Reword PRF.CPU.compiler to PGO profile data and recommendations. Make BLD.SYS.configs the sole owner of flag mechanism. Add per-module flag classes ('det-strict' owned by determinism-replay, 'perf'). Add optimization level, PGO and LTO to the XC.DET.conformance matrix on profile and shipping configs. Add non-responsibilities to cpu-performance.

findings.target: CORE.SCALE.actuators, C-SCALE, C-GOVERN, XC.DET.float, NET.SESS.overload, C-SIGNIF
findings.finding: The governor drives actuators (significance, animation rate, worker count, time dilation) from local, non-deterministic signals. Nothing classifies which actuators may change simulation-visible state. Under lockstep, rollback, server-authoritative play and replay, a client-local governor that alters sim tier, rate or worker count (reduction order) desyncs peers or invalidates recordings.
findings.evidence: Lockstep and rollback engines restrict adaptive quality to presentation. Server-side LOD changes are legitimate only as replicated authoritative state.
findings.proposed_change: Add an actuator class attribute to C-SCALE ('presentation' | 'sim-local-nonobservable' | 'sim-authoritative'). Under lockstep, rollback and replay recording only 'presentation' actuators are client-drivable. Sim-authoritative actuators go through tick-stamped events recorded as external inputs. Worker-count changes must not alter deterministic results, proven by XC.DET.conformance across core counts. Add capability CORE.SCALE.actuator-classes and a legacy pattern for client-local adaptive quality that alters simulation.

findings.target: PRF.METH.asymptotics, PRF.BENCH.scale-content, milestones M1/M5/M6, C-FRAME, C-FLOW, C-SPATIAL, C-VIEW, C-SIGNIF
findings.finding: Structural contracts that fix world-scale asymptotics are frozen at M1 on 2D indie games, but asymptotic declarations and stress worlds are first gated at M5/M6. Their validators are circular: M5 gates scale-content validated by asymptotics, and M6 gates asymptotics validated by scale-content. A scaling flaw found at M5 forces a breaking change to frozen contracts consumed by most skills. No scale probe runs before freeze.
findings.evidence: Late scale retrofits such as the Unity DOTS transform redesign and the UE world-partition retrofit. Production engines validate entity and streaming scaling on synthetic worlds before locking scheduler and data-flow interfaces.
findings.proposed_change: Add an M1 gate for PRF.METH.asymptotics (declaration) validated by PRF.BENCH.scale-content, plus an M1 scale-probe (1e6 entities, 1e4 cells, 64 cores, fitted slopes) as a precondition to freezing C-FRAME, C-FLOW, C-SPATIAL, C-VIEW and C-SIGNIF. Break the M5/M6 circularity by giving scale-content an independent oracle. Make 'asymptotic line declared' a freeze condition for every contract.

findings.finding: No capability owns parallel scalability: work/span and critical-path analysis of the compiled task graph, scheduling overhead per task and granularity, worker starvation, and core-count scaling curves (2 to 64 workers, SMT, P/E). C-GOVERN consumes a CPU critical-path signal that nothing produces or gates offline. Budgets fix one core count per tier, so serialization points that only appear on many-core CPUs go unseen.
findings.evidence: Work/span analysis is standard for task-graph engines (Naughty Dog fiber talk, Frostbite multithreading, UE Insights). Scaling caps above 16 threads and CCD splits on Threadripper and Zen exposed engine limits.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.CPU.parallel-scaling (owner cpu-performance; contributors job-system-task-graph, frame-orchestration, observability-telemetry): work/span extraction, scaling-curve benchmarks with core masks, per-task overhead limits, and a parallel-efficiency-at-N line in C-BUDGET. Add core-mask control to PRF.BENCH.lab. Add a serial-fraction budget for C-FRAME sync points and an M3 gate.

findings.target: C-BUDGET, PRF.METH.budgets, PRF.GPU.analysis, PRF.MEM.footprint, C-GOVERN, CORE.MEM.uma, OBS.LOG.hw-counters
findings.finding: UMA capacity is arbitrated but DRAM/fabric bandwidth is not a budget dimension. C-BUDGET has transfer bytes per frame (PCIe/staging) but no shared CPU+GPU memory bandwidth line. On consoles, Apple silicon, handhelds and mobile, bandwidth is often the binding limit, contended by GPU-driven culling, BVH refit, GPU decompression, streaming copies and CPU sim. The governor's CPU-vs-GPU-bound classification has no memory-bound class and picks wrong actuators.
findings.evidence: Console GDC talks on CPU-induced GPU bandwidth loss on shared GDDR6. Apple and Arm Mali/Immortalis bandwidth-counter guidance. Handheld PCs throttle on DRAM bandwidth.
findings.proposed_change: Add a DRAM/fabric bandwidth-per-frame line by consumer class to C-BUDGET for UMA and mobile tiers. Add PRF.MEM.bandwidth (owner memory-performance; contributors gpu-performance, loading-streaming-performance) using OBS.LOG.hw-counters. Add a memory-bound classification and bandwidth actuators (streaming rate, decompress throttle) to C-GOVERN and CORE.SCALE.actuators. Let RES.MGMT.arbitration hold a bandwidth budget as well as a capacity budget.

findings.target: PRF.METH.gates, PRF.BENCH.lab, PRF.BENCH.regression, C-BENCH, BLD.CI.device-lanes, BLD.CI.merge-queue
findings.finding: All perf gates are wall-clock measurements on exclusive, thermally conditioned reference hardware, including NDA devkits. With many parallel autonomous agents the lab is the scarcest resource. No cheaper pre-merge tier, lab scheduling or overload policy exists, so gates will be skipped, batched too coarsely to attribute, or become noisy statistical rejects.
findings.evidence: Chromium/V8 and Rust perf infrastructure use instruction-count proxies pre-merge and dedicated bots post-merge. Mozilla Perfherder and perf sheriffs tier the same way.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.BENCH.proxy-metrics (deterministic pre-merge proxies: instruction and cache-miss counts, allocations per frame, draw/dispatch/barrier counts, bytes per entity, memory traffic from replays, size-sweep complexity fits, calibrated against lab wall-clock). Add PRF.BENCH.lab-scheduling (queueing, risk priority, batching with bisect budget, NDA device allocation). Define gate tiers in PRF.METH.gates: pre-merge proxies, merge-queue lab subset, nightly full matrix. Track proxy calibration drift.

findings.target: milestones M2/M3/M4/M5, PRF.METH.energy, PRF.NET.resim-cost, PRF.MEM.size, PRF.NET.latency, PRF.NET.server-density
findings.finding: Milestone exits and gates are inconsistent with claimed obligations. M4 exit says server density is within budget, but PRF.NET.server-density is gated only at M6. Rollback at M2 has no PRF.NET.resim-cost gate. lite-3d mobile (M3) and xr-standalone (M5) have no energy or sustained-thermal gate. PRF.MEM.size (WASM and download size) and PRF.NET.latency are never gated.
findings.evidence: milestones.json gates list only PRF.MEM.footprint, pacing-latency, stats, GPU baselines, bandwidth, load-analysis, scale-content, asymptotics and server-density (M6). Sustained throttling is the dominant mobile failure mode.
findings.proposed_change: Add gates: M2 PRF.NET.resim-cost (validator QA.SIM.netsim), M2 PRF.MEM.size (PRF.BENCH.stats), M3 PRF.METH.energy (PRF.GPU.power), M4 PRF.NET.server-density and PRF.NET.latency (QA.FUNC.load), M5 PRF.METH.energy for xr-standalone. Keep M6 server-density for the AAA point.

findings.finding: C-BUDGET's summary lists no percentile frame-time (p99/p99.9), hitches-per-hour, stream-in speed at traversal speed, startup and transition time, or input-to-photon latency lines. Those exist only as analyzer capabilities. C-BENCH requires a C-BUDGET line reference per benchmark, so unlisted budgets cannot be referenced or gated.
findings.evidence: L70 forbids average-fps targets and pacing practice uses 1% and 0.1% lows and frame-time histograms (PresentMon).
findings.proposed_change: Extend C-BUDGET and PRF.METH.budgets with p50/p99/p99.9 frame time, max hitch length and hitches per hour per tier, startup and level-transition time, a traversal-speed by stream-in-quality line, and input-to-photon latency per refresh class and netcode family.

findings.finding: The catalogue has no pattern for fixed core-count and thread-per-subsystem designs (constant-sized worker pools, per-subsystem loops for physics, audio, streaming, network). It also lacks unbounded stage queues without back-pressure and benchmarking on non-profile builds. These are common defaults in agent-written code. L03 and L25 do not cover them.
findings.evidence: Thread-per-subsystem engines (Source, early Unreal, pre-DOTS Unity) capped scaling at the busiest subsystem and oversubscribed hybrid CPUs. Back-pressure is a requirement of DirectStorage-style pipelines.
findings.proposed_change: Add L75 'Thread-per-subsystem and fixed worker counts' (justification owner job-system-task-graph; stance_capabilities CORE.JOBS.thread-model, CORE.JOBS.scheduler, CORE.SCALE.actuators, PRF.CPU.hybrid). Add L76 'Unbounded stage queues and benchmarks on non-profile builds' (owner performance-architect; stance_capabilities RES.MGMT.pipeline, OBS.LOG.bench-runtime, PRF.METH.gates).

findings.target: ARCH.PROD (new ARCH.PROD.support-policy), BLD.CI.backports, XC.EXT.versioning, C-RELEASE, M7
findings.finding: No capability owns the engine support commitment: LTS duration, N-1 support, end-of-support dates, platform-SDK/store-mandate sunset and licensee migration deadlines. BLD.CI.backports owns mechanics, XC.EXT.versioning owns API deprecation and PLAT.PAL.os-support-policy owns OS versions, but nobody decides how long a stream is supported. The ladder ends at M7 'first LTS' with no post-1.0 lifecycle. Searching capabilities for sunset/EOL/support-window finds nothing engine-side.
findings.evidence: Unreal, Unity and Godot publish support windows that licensees plan multi-year titles against. Backport streams with no declared end grow without bound and drain agent budget.
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.PROD.support-policy (engine-product-management, E; contributors build-release-architect, api-lifecycle-migration, security-engineering) covering stream matrix, support window, EOL notice and platform-SDK sunset. Consume it from C-PROD/C-RELEASE. Add an M7 exit item 'EOL rehearsal of one release stream' and state that post-M7 work is cadence-driven.

findings.finding: cost-ledger only accounts for cost. No capability has authority to act on it: milestone budget envelope, burn/slip trigger, ordered descope list, stop/cancel criterion. Milestones have no time or cost box, and the risk register has no contingency response. Agents without a cut list will keep expanding scope.
findings.evidence: Production practice is a cut list and vertical-slice triage tied to milestone burn-down. The ladder is already ordered by configuration, so cuts can be expressed as unclaimed configurations.
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.ORG.scope-control (program-orchestration, E; contributors engine-architect, engine-product-management, cost-ledger).
