It defines a budget envelope per milestone, a burn/slip trigger, a descope order expressed as configurations and non-goals, and a human gate for envelope raise/cancel. Add these to ARCH.ORG.human-gates.

findings.finding: Every customer of the engine is agent-authored: reference games are written by the same organization against the public API and dogfood is internal. There is no external design-partner or early-access milestone, and intake/field-feedback have no real inflow until after M7. The API and its only validating games share the same blind spots.
findings.evidence: Frostbite's history of a shooter-tuned engine forced on RPG teams. Successful engines matured through real title teams (Fortnite for UE, Unity/Godot external alpha and beta programs).
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.PROD.design-partners (engine-product-management, E) covering recruitment per profile, agreements, feedback SLAs and support tiers. Add gates: M2 one external indie title on the public API, M4 one external multiplayer team, M7 at least N external titles on the release candidate. Register partner agreements as human gates and extend the external-reports untrusted input to partner projects.

findings.finding: The human-gate register names which decisions need a human but has no capacity model: no role roster (legal, security lead, platform account holder, product owner), no decision latency or queue, no batching, no delegate/expiry rule, and no policy for what agents do while blocked. Many gates are on the critical path (contracts, key custody, pen test, production rollout, NDA material), so humans are the throughput ceiling for N parallel agents.
findings.evidence: With automation in place, sign-off queues rather than build capacity set schedule. The framework sets SLAs for agent escalation but not for humans.
findings.proposed_change: Extend ARCH.ORG.human-gates or add ARCH.ORG.human-capacity: role roster, SLA per gate class, non-blocking continuation (gated task parks, agents proceed on independent work packages), batching cadence per milestone, delegate/expiry rule, and gate-wait-time metric in cost-ledger. Add a human_gate work-package type with owner role to C-ORCH.

findings.finding: External lead-time dependencies have no owner: platform-holder program admission and NDAs, devkit and hardware-lab procurement, certification/store-review queue slots, pen-test vendor booking, licensed middleware negotiation. M2 (console ship, TRC dry run), M4 (external pen test) and M7 (console certification pass) assume them. BLD.CI.devices schedules an existing fleet and PLAT.CON.devkit covers workflows, not acquisition.
findings.evidence: Console programs and cert slots take weeks to months and cannot be compressed by adding agents. Studios book kits and cert windows well before code-complete.
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.ORG.external-dependencies (program-orchestration, E; contributors platform-console, certification-compliance, ci-cd-automation): a lead-time register with start-by dates derived backwards from milestone exits, feeding ARCH.ORG.risk. Add a milestone entry precondition 'external item requested by M-1' and register procurement/agreement steps as human gates.

findings.finding: Inbound IP contamination is covered (snippet scan, clean-room policy). Outbound ownership is not: who holds copyright in an engine largely authored by agents, whether the licence is enforceable, who is licensor of record, what human-authorship record exists. licensing-model is owned by product management with no legal-review contributor. ARCH.ORG.provenance is not tied to any rights determination. Trademark/name clearance for the engine and sample assets is unowned.
findings.evidence: US Copyright Office guidance (2023-25): purely machine-generated material is not copyrightable and human authorship must be demonstrated, so a licence over such code may be unenforceable. Model-vendor output terms differ.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.CERT.authorship-ip (certification-compliance, E; contributor program-orchestration for provenance data) covering authorship records, model-vendor terms register, licensor of record and trademark clearance. Make certification-compliance a contributor to ARCH.PROD.licensing-model. Add 'licence, EULA and contributor terms published' to human-gates with a legal reviewer role, before M7.

findings.finding: Editor usability and creator documentation are validated only by agent-runnable oracles (iteration targets, doc snippet tests). Creator experience for artists, designers and audio staff cannot be judged by agents, and no milestone or human gate samples real creators, so 'content creators as users' is unverified.
findings.evidence: Editor UX failures are found in production by creator task observation, not by latency targets.
findings.proposed_change: Add a human creator-panel sampling gate per discipline at M2 (indie tools), M3 and M6 (team-large tools) with task-completion and time-to-first-asset thresholds. Register it in ARCH.ORG.human-gates, with ED.UI.ux as metric owner and developer-experience-docs as contributor.

findings.target: C-GPUTIER; skills.json profile hwrt; RND.GI.rt-required; RND.RHI.caps
findings.finding: C-GPUTIER models hardware as a linear ladder of named tiers ('rt', 'rt+tensor') and features declare a single minimum tier. RT, tensor/matrix, mesh, work-graph and binding capabilities are orthogonal and ship in different combinations (Metal 4 tensor without RT baseline, matrix units without a vendor-neutral tensor API, current consoles with RT but no tensor units). The hwrt profile text calls 'RT+tensor' the 'console baseline', which is only true of newer SKUs.
findings.evidence: DXR 1.x with SM 6.9 cooperative vectors, Vulkan cooperative matrix/vector, Metal 4 tensor ops are separate capability bits with different vendor availability.
findings.proposed_change: Reword C-GPUTIER so features declare a required capability set (API-neutral feature bits with versioned limits); tiers become named bundles for configurations and QA matrices. Reword hwrt to 'RT required, tensor only where a feature declares it' and drop 'console baseline'. Keep API mappings in RND.RHI.caps data, not in contract text.

findings.finding: Radar evidence and triggers are time-relative prose ('preview', 'beta', 'no shipped titles') with no as-of date, cited sources or staleness check, so maturity labels cannot be shown honest over a multi-year program and cannot be caught when stale. Labels such as cooperative-vector preview and work-graph 'no shipped titles' will flip within months, and radar status gates profile retagging.
findings.evidence: RND.SHADER.autodiff evidence 'SM 6.9 cooperative vectors (preview)'; RND.GEO.mesh-nodes 'no shipped titles'; reviews happen only at milestone exit.
findings.proposed_change: Add required fields reviewed (ISO date), evidence_refs (dated, typed T1-T6 sources) and per-class max_age_days (e.g. X/S 180, M 365); make check.py fail entries older than max age relative to the milestone date; express promotion triggers as testable predicates (shipped-title count, API status).

findings.target: PLAT.PAL.cloud-streaming; PLAT.PAL.cloud-hybrid; skills.json target/platform axes; C-PRESENT
findings.finding: Streaming-first delivery is modelled only for a build being streamed (session detection, touch overlay, UI scale). The engine-as-cloud-render-host case (headless GPU rendering, frame capture, low-latency hardware encode, video/input back-channel, multi-tenant GPU packing) has no owner or radar entry. headless-client is a non-rendering bot target, PLAT.SVC.capture is clip export, and encode appears only under hetero-offload (X).
findings.evidence: Unreal Pixel Streaming, NVIDIA CloudXR, GeForce NOW-style hosts, Omniverse streaming; hardware encode SDKs (NVENC/AMF/VideoToolbox) are established.
findings.proposed_change: Add capability PLAT.PAL.cloud-render-host (platform-architect, M; contributors frame-orchestration, gpu-platform-architect, network-transport, input-system), a radar entry (fallback: client build streamed by third-party host), a cloud-render-host target/platform value, and an encoder sink among C-PRESENT interposed presenters.

findings.target: RND.GEO.splats; CNT.IMP.splats; RND.GEO.splat-relight; radar splat entries
findings.finding: Three splat entries share identical evidence but carry different classes: static rendering is M while its required import is X, so a consumer sits in a higher class than its input path. M rests on research papers and an unstandardized glTF extension, not shipped-game evidence, a weaker bar than the radar applies to NTC or work graphs.
findings.evidence: Radar evidence is Kerbl 2023, 3DGRT 2024 and glTF extension work; fallback is photogrammetry meshes.
findings.proposed_change: Retag RND.GEO.splats to X (experimental) or split viewer (M) from gameplay renderer (X); align CNT.IMP.splats and RND.GEO.splats into one class or record why they differ.

findings.finding: Server meshing is M on one live deployment with sparse postmortems, while cloud-hybrid is X on one shipped title; the evidence bars are inconsistent. Meshing is bundled in persistent-world, so a shipping configuration inherits an unproven capability.
findings.evidence: docs/06 A5 admits one live deployment; radar revisit for meshing requires two shipped-title technical postmortems.
findings.proposed_change: Move NET.ARCH.meshing to X/experimental with zoning as the persistent-world requirement, or add one written evidence-to-class rule in radar _doc and apply it to both entries.

findings.finding: L73 calls upscaling and frame generation 'an optional presentation layer'. True for frame generation, not for upscaling: real-time path-traced and console 4K tiers are budgeted at internal resolution with reconstruction in the pipeline, and hwrt validates no raster fallback. A hwrt budget could omit the upscaler, or an ADR must hide a mandatory dependency as optional.
findings.evidence: Shipped path-traced titles and console performance modes are designed around internal resolution plus temporal upscaling and ray reconstruction.
findings.proposed_change: Split L73: frame generation stays optional and never counted toward latency/simulation budgets; upscaling becomes a declared budget input per tier (internal-resolution budget at base rate with reconstruction mode), mandatory where the tier declares it; add this to C-BUDGET tier records.

findings.target: non-goal GLES/WebGL backends; indie-2d configurations on web; RND.RHI.webgpu
findings.finding: Smallest 2D/card games claim web yet the web target requires WebGPU and the WebGL non-goal has no fallback; a sprite renderer needs none of WebGPU. The revisit trigger (>10% of a shipping audience lacking WebGPU) can only fire after shipping with no fallback; older WebViews and embedded browsers lag for years.
findings.evidence: WebGPU rollout 2023-2025 with uneven Linux/Android WebView tail.
findings.proposed_change: Keep WebGL out for std3d but allow a reduced-tier registered backend slot (or Canvas2D/WebGL2 path in render-2d-vector) for minimal/min2d web builds; or convert the trigger to a pre-ship gate using PLAT.WEB.audience-share at the web-release milestone.

findings.finding: No browser ML backend (WebNN, WebGPU-compute inference); the ml profile excludes web so browser ML NPCs/speech are cloud-only by omission. Volumetric/spatial video playback and light-field/holographic displays are absent from the radar.
findings.evidence: WebNN W3C Candidate Recommendation; ONNX Runtime Web on WebGPU; Apple Spatial Video.
findings.proposed_change: Add ML.RT.web-backends (M, platform-web, contributor ml-inference-runtime; fallback remote inference via C-LIVE) and radar S entries for volumetric/spatial video and light-field displays owned in RND and PLAT.XR.

findings.target: docs/06 A11; B29; CORE.LIFE.language; CORE.LIFE.interop; radar memory-safe entries
findings.finding: A11 limits memory-safe languages to parsers of untrusted data while B29/CORE.LIFE.language allow a mixed-language engine, and the radar trigger is only console toolchain support. None records that the implementers are autonomous agents, for whom language-enforced safety (borrow/bounds checking) makes UB classes machine-detectable; the 'hardened C++ plus fuzzing' fallback is presented as equivalent.
findings.evidence: Google Android memory-safety data (2024) tying vulnerability decline to new memory-safe code; C++ hardening modes are not language-enforced safety.
findings.proposed_change: Reconcile A11 with B29; add agent-verifiability and UB-class exposure as CORE.LIFE.language ADR criteria; add radar trigger 'agent-authored memory-safety escapes above threshold in C++ modules'.

findings.finding: No capability owns game-time timers / latent actions (delays, cooldowns, wait-N-seconds in level scripts, time-domain aware, pausable, saveable, replicated, deterministic). 'timer' appears only as hardware timer precision in PLAT.PAL.clocks. Systems will hand-roll wall-clock timers that break replay/rollback, are lost on save and ignore pause/dilation.
findings.evidence: UE TimerManager/latent actions, Unity coroutines/Invoke, Godot Timer are core modules of shipped engines; wall-clock timers desyncing replays is a classic bug class.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.SYS.timers owned by gameplay-systems-toolkit with contributors persistence-save, frame-orchestration, prediction-rollback; reference from GAM.SCR.level-scripting.

findings.finding: No startup crash-loop detection / safe-mode boot with automatic rollback of settings/mods to last-known-good when a config crashes before UI is reachable.
findings.evidence: Shipped PC titles offer reset-graphics-after-crash / safe launch; device-lost recovery and settings persistence exist but not this case.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.SCALE.safe-boot (runtime-scalability; contributors persistence-save, crash-diagnostics): crash marker, N-strike settings rollback, plugin/mod disable.

findings.finding: Skill lists 'virtual production' expertise but no capability covers genlock/frame-lock cluster rendering or timecode sync; not a radar non-goal, so neither owned nor excluded.
findings.evidence: UE nDisplay/ICVFX, simulators, venues need cluster sync and SMPTE timecode.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.ARCH.cluster-sync and ANM.CINE.timecode (M/X), or add an explicit non_goal and drop the expertise claim.

findings.finding: No IDE/debugger integration capability: compile_commands.json/project generation, debugger visualizers (natvis, lldb/gdb formatters) for handles, containers, entity ids, language-server support for script/data schemas.
findings.evidence: UE ships natvis and IDE project generators; Godot ships LSP; clangd-based agents need compilation databases.
findings.proposed_change: Add BLD.SYS.ide-integration (build-system-toolchains; contributors containers-core-types, scripting-runtime, developer-experience-docs) with a check that new handle/container types ship visualizers.

findings.finding: Time-gated events, daily/weekly resets and seasons have no owned calendar semantics (UTC vs local vs region time, DST, tzdata delivery on frozen platforms); timezone/calendar appears nowhere.
findings.evidence: DST/clock-change reset bugs are a standard live-service defect class; IANA tzdata changes several times a year and console OS copies lag.
findings.proposed_change: Extend PLAT.LIVE.events or add PLAT.LIVE.calendar owning time-zone/DST policy and tzdata delivery via remote config, with trusted-time as authority.

findings.target: CORE.FRAME.sim-schedule, ANM.ARCH.sync, C-FRAME, L01, docs/00 section 6
findings.finding: CORE.FRAME.sim-schedule says 'fixed sequence per tick; declared access used only for validation'. That is the central sequential update loop (L01) applied to the whole simulation. It contradicts CORE.FRAME.access-model and phases (ordering derived from declared access) and docs/00 section 6 ('canonical simulation dependency order'). It is not an adr_exception and is not in L01 stance_capabilities, so check.py cannot catch it. ANM.ARCH.sync inherits the wording.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to a canonical dependency order: a partial order derived from C-FRAME access declarations plus declared hard edges, with a deterministic tie-break. A total fixed sequence is allowed only per domain at determinism L2+ by ADR. Add the capability to L01 stance_capabilities, add contradiction_terms such as 'fixed sequence per tick', and align the C-FRAME summary and ANM.ARCH.sync.
findings.evidence: Determinism needs reproducible order, not a fixed sequence. Unity DOTS system ordering and Bevy schedules with ambiguity detection give deterministic DAGs. A fixed sequence serializes physics, animation, AI and navigation on many-core CPUs.

findings.target: legacy-patterns.json (new pattern), RND.GEO.precomputed-visibility, RND.GI.baked, RND.GI.lightmap-uv, RND.GI.bake-pipeline
findings.finding: No catalogue entry covers Quake-lineage static-world assumptions. Baked PVS/portal visibility and lightmap-only lighting are plain E capabilities with no tier restriction or stance. They conflict with destruction, time of day, runtime PCG and UGC worlds.
findings.proposed_change: Add pattern L75 'Baked static visibility/lighting as the world model'. Stance: dynamic GI and GPU/HZB occlusion on capable tiers, baked as a per-tier fallback with dynamic-object and invalidation rules (RND.ARCH.invalidation). Owner render-architect. stance_capabilities RND.GI.baked and RND.GEO.precomputed-visibility. Reword both capabilities as tier fallbacks.
findings.evidence: UE5 Lumen/Nanite, Frostbite and RE Engine default to dynamic GI and GPU occlusion. Baked GI and PVS remain as mobile and low-tier fallbacks.

findings.finding: Catalogue gaps with only implicit stances. (a) Thread-per-subsystem or per-connection blocking threads: L03 covers only game/render. (b) Wall-clock or sleep-based gameplay timers (L57 covers only tests). (c) Compiled-in fixed capacity caps. (d) Synchronous save or autosave that hitches the frame (L64 covers only the schema).
findings.proposed_change: Add entries with owners, stance_capabilities and contradiction_terms. 'Fixed per-subsystem or per-connection threads' -> pool plus pinned lanes (job-system-task-graph, CORE.JOBS.thread-model). 'Wall-clock gameplay timers' -> game-time timers on time domains (CORE.FRAME.time). 'Compiled-in capacity caps' -> budget-declared, config-sized pools (CORE.MEM.budget-enforcement). 'Synchronous save/autosave' -> async atomic snapshot save (GAM.SAVE.atomic).
findings.evidence: Thread-per-subsystem is the pre-2015 layout (UE3, early Source). Task-based engines replaced it. Async save is console certification guidance. Compiled-in caps break scale-up and scale-down.

findings.finding: L27 packs two new dogmas (ECS everywhere, GPU-driven everywhere) into one pattern anchored only to ARCH.GOV.adr, so it cannot be checked against CORE.OBJ.hybrid or RND.ARCH.submission-strategy. Other new dogmas are unrecorded: async-by-default physics (PHY.ARCH.async is E although rollback needs sync stepping), ML/neural replacing analytic techniques by default, and server-meshing/cloud-first by default.
findings.proposed_change: Split L27 into an ECS entry (stance_capabilities CORE.OBJ.hybrid, CORE.ECS.bridges) and a GPU-driven entry (RND.ARCH.submission-strategy). Add entries for 'neural/ML by default' and 'async physics by default', each with an evidence-ADR stance and an owner.
findings.evidence: The brief names new dogma explicitly. The current single entry has no capability anchor that check.py can verify.

findings.finding: L19 anchors only CORE.OBJ.events with a narrow regex. Contract text reintroduces callbacks: C-SEQ 'event/track callbacks'. C-ANIM animation events and C-PHYS contact events give no delivery mode. C-ID lists 'events' under identity.
findings.proposed_change: Reword C-SEQ to batched event outputs via C-FLOW/CORE.OBJ.events. State the delivery mode in C-ANIM and C-PHYS. Add these capabilities to L19 stance_capabilities. Add 'callbacks?' to L19 contradiction_terms with ADR exceptions. Remove 'events' from the C-ID summary.
findings.evidence: Synchronous anim notifies and sequencer event tracks that call gameplay mid-evaluation are the classic mutation-during-iteration and non-determinism source (UE anim notifies, Unity animation events).

findings.finding: No scale stance for the asset registry. A registry that is resident in full or scanned at boot is allowed. At open-world scale (millions of assets) that is the known Unreal AssetRegistry boot-time and memory problem, and there is no catalogue pattern for it.
findings.proposed_change: Add the pattern 'Full asset-registry scan or residency at boot'. Stance: cooked, chunked, on-demand registry with streamed indexes, and an incremental editor registry (ED.ARCH.scale). Owner content-pipeline-architect, stance_capabilities CNT.ID.registry. Reword CNT.ID.registry and C-ASSET.
findings.evidence: UE5 moved to on-demand registry state and chunked cook-time registries because of large-project scan time and memory.

findings.finding: 'World / level document format', 'Level transitions & seamless travel' and C-PCG 'per cell/chunk/level' keep the level as an authoritative unit, while WLD.MODEL.strategy, L18 and L39 stance the world as partitioned data. Level-as-file can re-enter as the default authoring and travel unit for 3D.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'World document (unit or partitioned)' and 'World-unit transition & seamless travel'. Add 'level' to L39 contradiction_terms, with an exception for minimal 2D configurations (WLD.MODEL.unit-load).
findings.evidence: Unreal's World Partition and One File Per Actor exist because level-as-file broke collaboration and streaming.

findings.finding: 'Shared / singleton components & resources' mirrors the hidden-global pattern. Nothing states that singletons are world-scoped, and CORE.ECS.singletons is not an L32 stance capability.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'World-scoped shared components/resources (no process-global singletons)'. Add the capability to L32 stance_capabilities.
findings.evidence: Bevy Resources and Unity singleton entities are per-World. Process-global ECS singletons break multi-world PIE, multi-instance servers and test isolation.

findings.finding: AUD.CONTENT.dialogue (VO playback and ducking for C-DIALOGUE lines) is owned by narrative-dialogue. narrative-dialogue lists 'VO playback -> audio-content-runtime' as a non-responsibility and facial-animation says 'Dialogue playback -> audio-content-runtime'. audio-content-runtime's purpose includes dialogue and VO. narrative-dialogue does not consume C-AUDIO, so its owner could not implement the row.
findings.evidence: The skills' own non_responsibilities contradict the capability row. Wwise/FMOD and UE dialogue-wave designs keep voice playback, priority and ducking in the audio layer and the line database in narrative.
findings.proposed_change: Set AUD.CONTENT.dialogue owner to audio-content-runtime with contributors [narrative-dialogue, localization-i18n]. Keep C-AUDIO out of narrative-dialogue.

findings.target: accessibility; UI.A11Y.*; QA.CERT.photosensitivity; post-color-hdr; vfx-particles; cinematics-sequencer
findings.finding: accessibility's purpose claims 'motion and photosensitivity options', but no capability implements them. The only photosensitivity row is QA.CERT.photosensitivity (late cert testing). There is no runtime flash/luminance/red-flash limiter or reduced-flash mode, no authoring-time flash analysis of VFX, cutscenes and UI, and no contract by which VFX, sequencer and UI honour such a setting.
findings.evidence: Harding / ITU-R BT.1702 and WCAG 2.3.1 (cited in docs/07); XAG and GAG flash-reduction guidance. Shipped titles (Fortnite, TLOU2, Forza) expose reduced-flash options because retrofitting is expensive.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.A11Y.photosensitivity (owner accessibility; contributors post-color-hdr, vfx-particles, cinematics-sequencer, ui-architect, certification-compliance) for the runtime limiter plus the C-A11YRT setting. Add a flash-analysis tool and a CNT.VAL validator on cooked sequences and VFX. Keep QA.CERT.photosensitivity as sign-off.

findings.target: narrative-dialogue; gameplay-data; cinematics-sequencer; gameplay-camera; input-system; CNT.VAL.submit-gate
findings.finding: ANM, AUD, PHY, AI/NAV, UI and A11Y each have a validation capability. The content-heavy domains have none: dialogue/narrative graphs (unreachable or dead-end nodes, soft-locks, fact/flag define-use, per-locale VO/caption/loc coverage), gameplay data (referential/range integrity), sequencer (binding and missing-track checks), camera (collision/clipping sweeps) and action maps (unbound actions, conflicting contexts). CNT.VAL.submit-gate says domain validators register via hooks, but nothing registers these.
findings.evidence: articy, Ink and Yarn linters and BG3-class dialogue tooling treat branch coverage and flag consistency as basic. Soft-locks are a leading defect class in narrative RPGs.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.NARR.validation (contributors localization-i18n, audio-content-runtime, accessibility), GAM.DATA.validation, ANM.CINE.validation, GAM.CAM.validation and INP.ACT.validation. Each registers with CNT.VAL.submit-gate and is oracle-authored outside its owner.

findings.target: CORE.FRAME.time; GAM.SYS.impacts; GAM.SYS.abilities; C-ABILITY; animation-runtime; audio-content-runtime; vfx-particles; gameplay-camera
findings.finding: Two feedback concerns are unowned. (1) Local time scale: CORE.FRAME.time covers only global real/game/dilation/pause, with no per-entity or per-team scale (hit-stop, bullet-time on a subset) obeyed consistently by animation, physics, VFX, audio, abilities and movement, and deterministic as frame data in rollback configs. (2) Gameplay cues: SYS.impacts routes only surface impacts, with no replicated, predicted, cosmetic-only cue channel fanning out from effects and abilities to VFX, audio, animation, camera shake and haptics with relevancy, LOD and rollback dedupe.
findings.evidence: UE Gameplay Cues (GAS, Lyra) are the shipped reference. Hit-stop is standard in action and fighting games (Street Fighter 6 frame data, Sakurai game-feel talks). Without an owner every subsystem invents its own timescale.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.FRAME.local-time-scale (frame-orchestration; contributors animation-architect, physics-architect, audio-content-runtime, vfx-particles, gameplay-architect) and GAM.SYS.cues (gameplay-systems-toolkit; contributors prediction-rollback, replication, gameplay-camera, input-devices-haptics). Extend C-ABILITY with the cue interface.

findings.target: C-ANIM; ANM.RT.blending; ANM.GRAPH.graph; ANM.TOOL.asset-editor; GAM.SYS.abilities; GAM.SYS.hit-detection
findings.finding: C-ANIM promises 'action/montage requests' and ANM.TOOL.asset-editor authors montages, but no runtime capability owns montages: gameplay-driven one-shots, slots layered into graphs, sections and jumps, blend in/out, root-motion policy inside a montage, or net-predicted and replicated montage state. Ability activation, hit windows and motion warping depend on it, so an authoring tool exists with no runtime owner.
findings.evidence: UE AnimMontage and slots, Unity playable-graph triggers, GAS AbilityTask_PlayMontage as the standard consumer.
findings.proposed_change: Add ANM.GRAPH.actions (owner animation-graphs; contributors animation-runtime, prediction-rollback, character-movement, gameplay-systems-toolkit) covering action/montage playback, slots, sections, notify-window ownership and replication participation. Reference it from ANM.TOOL.asset-editor.

findings.target: facial-animation (profiles lite3d/std3d); ANM.FACE.lipsync; ANM.RT.2d; narrative-dialogue; minimal and min2d configurations
findings.finding: FACE.lipsync (per-locale) lives only in facial-animation, tagged lite3d/std3d. The minimal profile (narrative-centric) and min2d carry VO, C-DIALOGUE and per-locale VO packs but have no audio-driven mouth/expression driving for 2D portraits and sprites, and no portrait/expression-layer staging or text reveal synced to VO. Visual novels and 2D RPGs would rebuild this per game, and per-locale retiming is unsolved for them.
findings.evidence: Ren'Py, Live2D Cubism audio-driven lip-sync parameters, Spine mouth-shape slots; standard in the indie and mobile VN market the minimal profile targets.
findings.proposed_change: Add ANM.FACE.lipsync-2d (owner facial-animation with profile addition for min2d and minimal, or owner animation-runtime; contributors audio-content-runtime, narrative-dialogue) and GAM.NARR.staging-2d (portrait/expression layers, text reveal timing). Widen or split the facial-animation profiles.

findings.target: GAM.FW.rules; GAM.AI.search; NET.ARCH.async; NET.ARCH.async-validation; character-movement; minimal profile
findings.finding: The minimal profile targets card and narrative games and async turn-based play is a named add-on. AI.search needs clonable rule state and NET.ARCH.async-validation re-simulates submitted results. No capability defines a turn/phase/command-log substrate (ordered commands, undo/history, deterministic state cloning, command-log replay). There is also no grid/tile discrete-movement mode; MOVE.platformer is the only 2D mode.
findings.evidence: 4X, tactics, roguelike, card (Slay the Spire, Hearthstone) and mobile async titles are built on a command/turn queue. Without an owner, AI, validator, replay and save each invent it.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.FW.turns (gameplay-architect; contributors determinism-replay, ai-behavior-perception, persistence-save, online-services-liveops) with a clonable-state API, and GAM.MOVE.grid (character-movement).

findings.target: GAM.SAVE.model; GAM.SAVE.platform; GAM.SAVE.migration; PLAT.SVC.user-model; ugc configurations
findings.finding: Persistence rows omit (a) tolerating or preserving unknown content when a mod or DLC that wrote data is absent, (b) a save-slot catalogue with locale-independent metadata (playtime, thumbnail, version) for load UIs and cross-platform portability, and (c) binding save ownership to the platform user, guests and split-screen locals, which exists only as a contributor line on PLAT.SVC.user-model. The ugc configurations claim mods with no save-compat rule.
findings.evidence: Skyrim and Fallout 4 script-baked saves orphaned by mod removal; Minecraft and Factorio mod-mismatch handling; console cert requirements on per-user save handling.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.SAVE.unknown-content (unknown-record preservation and quarantine, mod/DLC dependency manifest per save; contributors modding-ugc, serialization-schema) and GAM.SAVE.slots (metadata, thumbnails, per-user ownership, portability; contributors platform-services, ui-architect). Include both in QA.FUNC.compat-corpus scope.

findings.finding: No interaction and target-selection system exists: interactable discovery and focus, hold-to-interact, contextual prompts with the active device glyph and localized text, soft-target and lock-on selection, and arbitration among candidates and local players. AI smart objects exist but their player-facing counterpart (input, prompt UI, animation and motion-warp handshake) is unowned, so each game rebuilds it across input, UI and abilities.
findings.evidence: UE Lyra interaction system, Unity XR Interaction Toolkit, lock-on targeting as core action-RPG infrastructure.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.SYS.interaction (gameplay-systems-toolkit; contributors input-system, ui-architect, animation-runtime, gameplay-camera) covering candidate scoring, prompt model and lock-on target set, server-validated for online configurations.

findings.finding: AUD.ARCH.devices is a single row. Not named: endpoint change and hot-swap (headset, Bluetooth, HDMI) with sample-rate and channel-layout renegotiation; multi-endpoint output (main mix plus per-local-player controller speaker or headset for split-screen and couch co-op); OS interruption and focus policy (calls, minimize, console suspend). PLAT.PAL.system-events lists audio endpoints as an event source but no audio owner consumes them.
findings.evidence: PS5 DualSense speaker and headset routing, Xbox per-user audio endpoints, iOS AVAudioSession interruptions (a cert item); a common source of stuck-silent audio bugs.
findings.proposed_change: Add AUD.ARCH.routing (audio-architect; contributors platform-architect, platform-console, input-devices-haptics, gameplay-architect) and list it as a consumer of PLAT.PAL.system-events.

findings.finding: Text input is a single row. The editing model is unowned: caret, selection, extended grapheme clusters (UAX #29, emoji ZWJ, Indic conjuncts), bidi caret movement, password and character-limit fields. TXT.bidi cites only UAX #9 and #14. UI.LOC.cldr is named 'formatting', so collation, case folding, normalization and accent-insensitive search (sorting names and item lists) are unassigned.
findings.evidence: Unicode UAX #29 and UAX #10; chat-field behaviour in Slack and Discord. Truncating by code unit breaks emoji and Hindi text.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.TXT.editing (owner text-fonts; contributors ui-architect, platform-architect, accessibility), UI.TXT.segmentation (UAX #29) and UI.LOC.collation (localization-i18n).

findings.target: legacy-patterns.json (L72 stance_capabilities; new patterns); navigation-pathfinding; text-fonts
findings.finding: The legacy catalogue lacks four recurring stances in these domains: ASCII, bitmap-font or code-unit text without shaping/bidi/grapheme handling; sentence assembly by string concatenation (L72's stance names plural/gender but stance_capabilities lists only UI.LOC.strings, not UI.LOC.messageformat or UI.LOC.terms); synchronous per-agent path requests and main-thread navmesh rebuilds; designer tunables as code constants.
findings.evidence: ICU/CLDR guidance on concatenation and code-unit failures; Detour/Recast and Mass AI use batched, budgeted queries; hard-coded tunables are the antithesis of GAM.DATA.tuning.
findings.proposed_change: Add L75 (text without shaping or grapheme awareness; UI.TXT.shaping, UI.TXT.bidi), L76 (sentence concatenation; UI.LOC.messageformat, UI.LOC.terms), L77 (sync per-request pathfinding and rebuild; GAM.AI.pathfinding, GAM.AI.navmesh), L78 (hard-coded tunables; GAM.DATA.tuning). Fix L72's stance_capabilities.

findings.finding: Purpose text and ownership diverge, so generated SKILL.md files would conflict. The toolkit's purpose lists 'gameplay tags' but GAM.DATA.tags is owned by gameplay-data, whose purpose omits tags. The toolkit purpose omits hit detection, projectiles, building, aim assist, volumes, impacts and markers. UI.FW.maps needs a cook step and a top-down capture but its contributors omit asset-cook-processors and render-architect.
findings.evidence: skills.json purpose strings versus capabilities.json owners and contributors.
findings.proposed_change: Move 'gameplay tags' from the toolkit purpose to gameplay-data and rewrite the toolkit purpose to cover its owned areas. Add asset-cook-processors and render-architect as contributors to UI.FW.maps. If the toolkit becomes too broad, split combat systems (hit-detection, projectiles, aim-assist) from world systems (volumes, markers, building, impacts).

findings.finding: A11Y.assists (assist and difficulty hooks) and DATA.tuning (difficulty variants) share territory with no mutual contributor entry. Nothing defines how per-player assists (extended timers, auto-aim, invulnerability) are scoped in multiplayer: authoritative versus local, allowed in competitive queues, flagged on leaderboards and achievements. Simulation-affecting assists must be replicated and validated.
findings.evidence: TLOU2 and Celeste assist modes; competitive modes disable some assists; XAG difficulty and co-op guidelines.
findings.proposed_change: Add gameplay-data as contributor of UI.A11Y.assists and accessibility as contributor of GAM.DATA.tuning. Extend UI.A11Y.assists with an assist-class attribute (cosmetic, input-only, simulation-affecting), require simulation-affecting assists to be replicated and recorded, and add a score-integrity flag consumed by XC.SEC.score-integrity.

findings.target: data/milestones.json (M0-M7 skills/contracts_frozen/gates); test-architect, robustness-fuzzing, simulation-validation, render-validation, functional-automation-soak, certification-compliance, security-engineering
findings.finding: No milestone lists any process skill in `skills`. M0 freezes C-MEM, C-SYNC, C-TASK, C-MATH and other contracts whose oracle_author is robustness-fuzzing. M0 gates name validators owned by simulation-validation, certification-compliance and test-architect. None of these skills arrives in any milestone. check.py closure covers runtime skills only, so 'frozen after owner and a consumer' never checks that the oracle author and gate validator exist by then.
findings.evidence: contracts.json oracle_author; milestones.json M0 skills list contains only ci-cd-automation and test-runtime-harness from the QA side; the walking-skeleton proof is vacuous for the validation side.
findings.proposed_change: Add per-milestone process_skills (or allow process skills in skills). Check that every contract drafted or frozen at Mk has its oracle_author, and every gate's owner and validator owner, present at or before Mk. Schedule test-architect, robustness-fuzzing, simulation-validation and render-validation at M0, functional-automation-soak at M1, certification-compliance at M1 or M2.

findings.target: data/milestones.json gates (QA.AGENT.holdout, QA.AGENT.mutation-gate, QA.AGENT.gate-canaries, XC.SEC.agent-boundary, QA.STRAT.release-criteria, QA.FUNC.compat-corpus, PRF.BENCH.scale-content, PRF.METH.asymptotics)
findings.finding: Gate validators are not independent and often do not exercise the property validated. About 28 gates have owner and validator in the same workstream (security-engineering and privacy-data-protection sit in quality). Circular pairs: gate-canaries vs agent-boundary; QA.FUNC.soak vs PRF.MEM.footprint; scale-content vs asymptotics; release-criteria to compat-corpus to prechecks. The sealed holdout is validated by QA.SIM.golden-traces, which cannot show implementers cannot read it; the mutation gate is validated by fuzzing, not seeded weak tests. Gates carry no pass criterion.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL 'builder never grades its own fixes'; framework claim 'a guard never seen to fail is not a guard'; gate objects contain only capability and validator, criteria are prose in exit.
findings.proposed_change: Extend gate schema to {capability, validator, kind, criterion (metric, threshold, evidence-bundle item)}. Require validator owner workstream different from capability owner workstream and forbid 2-cycles and triangles. Re-pair holdout to a red-team read attempt (agent-redteam plus BLD.CI.sealed-suites) and mutation-gate to seeded weak-test injection. Move security-engineering and privacy-data-protection to assurance.
